pages.title: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander liaison services
pages.html:
Proposed service overview

This service page is intended to help staff find culturally appropriate liaison support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients and families in Bagwan scenarios.

Discuss the person's needs

Ask about the person's preferences for support and communication. Respect their choice about involving family, support people or a liaison service. Discuss the relevant referral arrangements with the scenario facilitator.

Liaison team

The archived staff directory names Gina Starr, Fiona Phillips, Monti Williams and Merindah Olden. Their formal reporting lines await confirmation.

Service details awaiting confirmation

Referral processes, hours, contact details and responsibilities need to be developed with the cultural safety SME. The service description must be reviewed for cultural appropriateness before teaching use.

Available resource

The recovered Closing the Gap video is available in the video library as a discussion resource.

pages.html:
Interpreting booking form

Policies and procedures

Interpreting, language services rights and responsibilities 

Booking an interpreter 

What Government policies and procedures have informed Bagwan Health’s interpreting services?

Bagwan Health has used the following government policies and procedures to inform how we deliver our interpreting services. These include:

  • Interpreting services — Victorian Government policy
  • Victorian Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) language services policy and guidelines
  • Using interpreting services — Victorian Government guidelines
  • NSW Health policy on working with interpreters
  • Working with interpreters  
  • Assessing the need for an interpreter

How to translate health information into different languages.

The Victorian Government Health Translations website enables patients and interpreters the ability to translate health and wellbeing information into over 100 languages to ensure it is more accessible to people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Should we use family, relatives, friends and/or bilingual staff as interpreters?

Never! Using family, relatives, friends and/or bilingual staff (that are not registered interpreters) to interpret any health information is both a breach of:

  • the official Standard Procedures
  • our duty of care owed to the patient/client, and could result in legal action.

Interpreting interactive personal development activity 

Bagwan Health have created an interactive PD activity on crucial decision points for interpreters.

Interpreting interactive activity

Victorian interpreter assistance cards.

Download the Victorian Interpreter Cards Zip file in here. Help Victorians with limited English to access government services. The wallet-sized card can be used by people with limited English ability to:

  • request interpreter assistance
  • help staff to understand what language they need to arrange language assistance for.

The card features the National Interpreter Symbol.

pages.title: Interpreting interactive professional development activity
pages.html:
In conjunction with some of the interpreting team, Bagwan Health have scripted, filmed and created an excellent short professional development activity. All staff are welcome to complete this to work through some crucial decision points that interpreters face.

The following professional development activity is an excellent introduction to when interpreters face crucial ethical and professional decision points and how they can best deal with these.

Select ‘Start scenario’ to begin the professional development activity. By the end of this module you will be able to clearly identify several key decision points when interpreting for clients in a health context.

Branching scenario

Objective

Simulated scenarios for the user to practice knowledge and skills. Scenarios relate to best practice, ethics, and code of conduct related to accredited interpreter. The activity will have question and decision points along the way using film/videos of scenarios and decision outcomes.

Context for scenarios

Consultation with specialist doctor – Cardiologist to discuss medical results. Dialogue to revolve around medical results for Patient. Doctor diagnoses high-cholesterol based on latest blood test, and advises Patient how to manage high blood pressure better.

Characters in scenario include:

Interpreter Cardiologist Mrs Trang (patient) Parker (grandson)

 

 

  • Next

Introduction 

This activity promotes best practice on how to establish a interpreter-client relationship. 

You will assume the role of a an interpreter. You’re assigned to interpret a medical consultation between doctor and patient.

Based on code of conduct related dilemmas, you will face decision points on how to proceed along the way.

Please note: The scenarios presented are a fictional account to represent ethical issues. Any resemblance to actual persons is unintentional.

 

  • Next

How it works

  • Watch interactions between client, community doctor, and certified interpreter.
  • After each interaction, you are to select the most appropriate response. Possible response outcomes can be either : A good approach or not the best approach
  • You can redo and repeat this activity many times to practice and to improve your responses.
  • This activity has sound, so please adjust your volume as needed.

This activity uses high resolution videos for each scenario. For best results, please use high-speed Internet connectivity.

  • Next

Video scenario– Start – Competence

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 4 on YouTube

 

Patient with family member have already registered at reception and have arrived at Cardiologist consultation appointment at opened room entrance door.

Family member advises Cardiologist that they don’t require an interpreter for the consultation as they believe they are able to interpret instead (despite already been agreed to, arranged, and booked).

  • Next

How do you proceed? 

  • A. Client requires an accredited interpretor. Wait for accredited interpretor to join.
  • B. Family member can interpret for Patient during consultation.
  • C. Replay previous video

Video outcome A

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 6 on YouTube

An interpretor’s role is to help improve communication, and clinical outcomes, providing satisfaction with care in patients with limited English proficiency.

 

  • Next

Video outcomes B

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 7 on YouTube

 

Not the best result

If family members, friends or staff who are not trained as accredited interpreters try to interpret, risks are that errors in understanding and communication are more likely to occur. This can pose grave risks to the patient as well as liability to the healthcare provider or institution.

  • Try again

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 8 on YouTube

Accredited interpretor arrives at consultation room for appointment, and is met by the Cardiologist at the entrance. Caridologist is waiting impatiently for interpretor to arrive.

  • Next

How do you proceed?

  • A. Debrief with Cardiologist prior to entering the room to obtain additional context and background information to booking request.
  • B. Basic content is already provided on booking request form. Enter room to immediately begin consultation
  • C. Replay previous video

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 10 on YouTube

Good feedback for best practice to support optimal interpretation outcomes during the session: Source content description.

  • Next

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 11 on YouTube

Bad feedback: Source content description

 

  • Try again

Consider incorporating a break for long sessions.  

As with all interpreting, it is important to be patient and allow time for communication due to the delay between a message being spoken or signed and the interpretation.

  • Next

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 13 on YouTube

 Dialogue turns to advice from Cardiologist on how to manage high blood pressure better otherwise Patient health will suffer further will need to arrange follow up consultation to track progress and health improvement.

Family member does not wish to have information shared with Patient about any health scare, and wishes to have the health management information filtered to sound ‘not as serious’ as not to upset the Patient with the result details.

  • Next

How do you proceed?

  • Option A – will be ‘good’ ideal outcome
  • Option B – will be ‘bad’ not a great outcome
  • Replay video

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 15 on YouTube

  • Next

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 16 on YouTube

  • Try again

Watch Interpreting scenario — step 17 on YouTube

 

Thank you and farewell between all the parties.

pages.title: Laboratory PPE reference
pages.html:
Use the task risk assessment

Select protective equipment using the approved procedure and the hazards of the task. The original activity's single set of clothing choices does not establish suitable PPE for every laboratory task.

Before work

  • Confirm the task, hazards and approved controls.
  • Check the specified protective clothing, hand protection, eye protection and footwear.
  • Check that equipment fits, is in good condition and is suitable for the task.
  • Clarify any missing instruction with the supervisor before proceeding.

Practical skills

Selection, fit, use and removal require supervised practice. The optional HTML exercise is in the learning guide and does not assess practical competence.

pages.title: Laboratory waste reference
pages.html:
Identify the waste before disposal

Use the current local waste procedure and the labels on the approved containers. Waste classification depends on what the material is and what it is contaminated with.

When information is missing

Do not guess from a picture or container colour. Ask the supervisor to confirm the classification and handling requirements.

Archived activity correction

The original activity described expired medication without specifying its type. That description does not establish that the medication is cytotoxic. The draft practice exercise uses an explicitly identified cytotoxic residue instead. The SME must review every category and example before use.

Bagwan Health is excited to announce the launch of their new brand appearance and their new, staff intranet.

Over the past few months, we have been working to come up with a new logo and brand appearance that is fresh, modern and professional.

In addition, we are launching our intranet, which, apart from having a clean and colourful new look, is now much more focused on connecting staff with internal communications.

Features of the intranet include:

• Staff organisation chart
• Easy access to forms templates and policies and procedures
• Quick access to the secured patient database and incident reporting forms.

Bagwan Health’s branding has been chosen to give a welcoming and inclusive energy to all of our facilities communications.

pages.title: Free cultural awareness training
pages.html:
Did you ever want to learn more about how your cultural biases can impact on your professional judgement? Did you know that effective communication can mean different things with people from different cultures? As a part of our partnership with RMIT University we are able to offer three credentials for our staff to complete.

The following are three excellent micro-credentials available to Bagwan Health staff as a part of our partnership with RMIT University.

Select the title to reveal links to content from these training.

In this course you will learn how to:

  • Analyse, evaluate and articulate the implications of diversity based on their own experiences
  • Recognise the role of one’s own values and behaviour in response to different cultural experiences
  • Reflect on past experiences through a cultural intelligence lens
  • Create a roadmap for developing further cultural intelligence
  • Ask questions of peers to uncover and reflect on cultural differences.

Sign up to Building Cultural Intelligence now.

In this course you will learn how to:

  • Recognise different type of biases, in particular unconscious bias
  • Provide examples of unconscious bias at the workplace and how they can have a negative impact on work productivity
  • Distinguish between stereotypes and generalisations
  • Critically analyse how assumptions, biases and stereotypes can lead to prejudice and discrimination
  • Apply core behaviours (curiosity, respect and empathy) and practices essential to successful cross-cultural interaction.

Start Overcoming Bias and Assumptions now.

In this course you will learn how to:

  • Identify how different cultures view the concept of time
  • Explain how communication styles may be influenced by cultures
  • Describe how to use cultural similarities to initiate and build a relationship
  • Recognise the differences and similarities amongst diverse cultures.

Start Cultural Differences and Similarities now.

pages.title: Influenza outbreak
pages.html:
Bagwan Health recently experienced an influenza outbreak. Although it was controlled and maintained quickly, it’s important that all staff follow standard infection control standards:

• Hand hygiene and cough etiquette

• Use of personal protective equipment (PPE)

• Safe use and disposal of sharps

• Routine environmental cleaning

• Incorporation of safe practices for handling blood, body fluids and secretions as well as excretions.

 Review the Infection Control Policy and Procedure Test your knowledge on waste management to reduce the risk of infection

The People and Culture team spend their time ensuring we support our people, so they can deliver outstanding patient care and achieve excellent patient outcomes. Our priorities are around growing leadership and management capabilities to take our organisation into the future. We also support our leaders in designing and implementing changes that promote efficiency and excellence.

pages.title: Our community
pages.html:
Welcome to Bagwan Health

Chief executive officer Dr. Christina Jones welcomes you to Bagwan Health and encourages you to take a look at Bagwan Health’s core values.

Watch Welcome to Bagwan Health on YouTube

Our values

Our five core values guide how we work together.

Compassion

We treat everyone with kindness and care.

Excellence

We are committed to learning and innovation.

Integrity

We are open, honest and fair.

Unity

We work together for the benefit of all.

Respect

We treat everyone with respect and dignity at all times.

Our vision

Bagwan Health has grown from the core belief in the dignity in care for every human being. Our vision is to be the first in care, research and learning, to help improve the life and health for our community. We entrust our core beliefs to everyone involved at Bagwan Health.  You can see and experience the vision of Bagwan Health come to life everyday through our services and our people.

Cultural diversity

At Bagwan Health we aim to provide the best possible experience for our whole community.

We believe that by providing a safer more inclusive workplace contributes to our success in bringing the best care to our patients, families and wider community.

Learn about cultural diversity in the workplace

Our equal opportunity policy

This policy demonstrates Bagwan Health’s commitment to promoting equal opportunity to all staff. Equal opportunity law aims to promote everyone’s right to equal opportunities.

All staff need to comply with all of its obligations. 

Read our equal opportunity policy

Interpreting interactive personal development activity 

Bagwan Health have created an interactive PD activity on crucial decision points for interpreters.

Interpreting interactive activity

Victorian interpreter assistance cards.

Download the Victorian Interpreter Cards Zip file in here. Help Victorians with limited English to access government services. The wallet-sized card can be used by people with limited English ability to:

  • request interpreter assistance
  • help staff to understand what language they need to arrange language assistance for.

The card features the National Interpreter Symbol.

Policies and procedures

Interpreting, language services rights and responsibilities 

Booking an interpreter 

What Government policies and procedures have informed Bagwan Health’s interpreting services?

Bagwan Health has used the following government policies and procedures to inform how we deliver our interpreting services. These include:

  • Interpreting services — Victorian Government policy
  • Victorian Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) language services policy and guidelines
  • Using interpreting services — Victorian Government guidelines
  • NSW Health policy on working with interpreters
  • Working with interpreters  
  • Assessing the need for an interpreter

How to translate health information into different languages.

The Victorian Government Health Translations website enables patients and interpreters the ability to translate health and wellbeing information into over 100 languages to ensure it is more accessible to people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds.

Should we use family, relatives, friends and/or bilingual staff as interpreters?

Never! Using family, relatives, friends and/or bilingual staff (that are not registered interpreters) to interpret any health information is both a breach of:

  • the official Standard Procedures
  • our duty of care owed to the patient/client, and could result in legal action.

Use the organisation's approved language service arrangements. Confirm the interpreter's suitability and credentials for the task. Provide the information required for the booking through the approved channel and confirm the arrangements with the patient and the appointment team.

Plan suitable space, equipment and time. Brief the interpreter on the purpose and relevant context. Check that the patient understands the interpreter's role.

pages.policy_document: documents/policies-and-procedures/Bagwan Health - Bullying and Harassment, V1.0.docx
pages.html:
Policy Name Bullying and Harassment

Scope

This policy applies to all Bagwan Health Staff, whether employees, contractors or volunteers, Allied Health professionals, Credentialed Specialists, students, patients and visitors.

Policy

Bagwan Health is committed to providing a positive working environment free from bullying and harassment. Bagwan Health will not tolerate threatening behaviour and this includes intimidation, bullying, harassment, physical violence, victimisation and isolation in the workplace.

The purpose of this policy is to create awareness and to minimise the risk of bullying and harassment in the work environment.

Procedure

Responsibilities 

Everyone in the workplace has a responsibility to ensure that the workplace is free of any harassment, discriminatory or bullying behaviour.

Bagwan Health is responsible for providing a workplace that promotes the health and well-being of all staff, students, patients and visitors.

Staff have duties under the OHS Act to take reasonable care of their own health and safety, as well as the health and safety of others in the workplace. They must cooperate in any action taken by their employer to comply with measures ensuring health and safety. 

This policy complies with the following legislation.

Federal jurisdiction: 

·         Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission Act 1986

·         Sex Discrimination Act 1984

·         Racial Discrimination Act 1975

·         Disability Discrimination Act 1992

·         Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012 (WGE Act)

·         Age Discrimination Act 2004

·         Fair Work Act 2009

State jurisdiction:

·         The Victorian Equal Opportunity Act 2010

·         Racial and Religious Tolerance Act 2001

·         Victorian Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities 2006

·         Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004

·         Crimes Act 1958 (including Brodie’s Law) 

Bullying and Harassment in the Workplace

Bullying and Harassment in the workplace can take place between:

·         A worker and a manager (or team leader)

·         Co-workers

·         A worker and another person in the workplace, e.g. a patient.

What is Workplace Bullying?

Bullying at work, as defined by the Fair Work Act 2009, occurs when – a person or a group of people behave unreasonably and repeatedly, towards a worker or a group of workers, while at work – and the behaviour creates a risk to health and safety.

Bullying can occur wherever people work together. Under certain conditions, most people are capable of bullying. Because bullying at work is an occupational health and safety hazard, the intent is not relevant to the definition.

Bullying has three main features:

1. It involves a misuse of power in a relationship.

2. It is ongoing and repeated.

3. It involves behaviours that can cause harm.

Bullying behaviours can include:

·         Verbal abuse

·         Putting someone down

·         Spreading rumours or innuendo about someone

·         Interfering with someone’s personal property or work equipment

·         Unjustified criticism or complaints

·         Deliberately excluding someone from workplace activities

·         Deliberately denying access to information or other resources

·         Withholding information that is vital for effective work performance

·         Setting tasks that are unreasonably above or below a staff member’s ability

·         Deliberately changing work arrangements, such as rosters and leave, to inconvenience a particular staff member

·         Setting timelines that are very difficult to achieve

·         Excessive scrutiny at work.

 

What is Workplace Harassment?

Harassment is any form of behaviour that is not wanted, not asked for and not returned which makes the receiver feel:

·         Humiliated

·         Offended

·         Intimidated.

Harassment can take many shapes and can involve actions, comments, behaviour or physical contact. Under federal and state legislation, unlawful harassment occurs when someone is made to feel intimidated, insulted or humiliated because they have any of the characteristic specified under anti-discrimination or human rights legislation.

Harassing behaviour can range from serious to a less serious nature, however, one-off incidents can still constitute harassment if there is an occurrence of:

·         Unwanted physical contact, such as touching or fondling

·         Suggestive behaviours, such as leering or ogling

·         Kissing or embracing someone against their will

·         Unnecessary familiarity such as deliberately brushing up against someone

·         Unwanted comments about a person’s sex life or physical appearance

·         Suggestive remarks, sexual jokes, innuendoes, lewd comments

·         Sexual propositions or continual requests for dates

·         Displaying and using offensive objects, written material, pornographic or sexually suggestive pictures

·         Continual requests for something when the person has made it clear they are not interested in participating.

Reasonable Managerial Actions

Reasonable actions performed in a reasonable way are not bullying; examples include:

·         Setting performance goals, standards and deadlines

·         Allocating work to a staff member

·         Transferring a staff member

·         Deciding not to select a staff member for promotion

·         Informing a staff member about unsatisfactory work performance

·         Informing a staff member about inappropriate behaviour

·         Implementing organisational changes

·         Performance management processes

·         Constructive feedback

·         Downsizing. 

Other Types of Bullying
Reactive or Isolated Incidents of Bullying

This type of bullying is where stressful circumstances, stemming from personal or workplace issues result in a deterioration of behaviour. In reaction, a staff member may become short-tempered and irritable. Where a staff member reacts adversely, he or she will often recognise the inappropriateness of their behaviour.

The staff member should apologise and learn from the experience so that any adverse behaviour is avoided in the future. In some cases, the staff member may need to be counselled to understand that their behaviour is not acceptable.

If a staff member continues to exhibit inappropriate behaviour over a period of time in response to stress, this behaviour may fall under the general bullying category and appropriate action will be taken.

Serial bullying

This is the most serious type of workplace bullying. Serial bullying is identified when a staff member targets numerous coworkers in succession.

Bullying and Discrimination

Bullying may also be discrimination if it is because of a person’s age, sex, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, pregnancy or certain other reasons. Sexual harassment and racial hatred are also against the law.

Bullying does not include:

·         Occasional differences of opinion and non-aggressive conflicts and problems in working relations

 

·         Workplace counselling, managing underperformance and other actions in accordance with the staff member’s employment conditions or policies.

The behaviour will only be defined as bullying if a reasonable person observing the situation would consider it to be bullying.

Responsibilities of Managers

Managers must ensure that all staff understand that bullying is not tolerated in the workplace and must take early corrective action to deal with behaviour that may be offensive or intimidating.

If a manager feels that a reported incident might constitute bullying and feels that the nature of the complaint is outside their expertise, they can refer the matter to the Corporate Services Manager. The prevention of all inappropriate behaviours including bullying requires managers to:

·         Be aware of and identify bullying in the workplace

·         Eliminate inappropriate behaviour regardless of whether a complaint is received about that behaviour

·         Encourage all staff to behave in accordance with the principles of equal opportunity and anti-discrimination

·         Provide leadership and role modelling in relation to appropriate and professional behaviour in the workplace

 

·         Respond promptly, sensitively and confidentially to all situations where inappropriate behaviour is exhibited or alleged to have occurred.

Responsibilities of Staff 

All staff have a moral responsibility to help create a positive and safe workplace. The prevention of all inappropriate behaviours including bullying requires staff to:

·         Be aware of and identify bullying

·         Behave in accordance with the principles of equal opportunity and anti-discrimination

·         If bullying behaviour is witnessed or experienced, and the staff member feels able, speak with the alleged bully to object to the bullying behaviour

·         Tell the person that is bullied about the steps they can take to solve it

·         Offer to act as a witness if the person being bullied decides to report the incident

 

·         Keep a record or diary of incidents, noting what happened, when and the names of witnesses.

Where to Seek Advice?

·         Senior management

·         Program manager

·         Team leader

·         Coordinator

·         Occupational health and safety committee member

·         Union representative

·         Victorian Equal Opportunity & Human Rights Commission

Enquiries: 1300 292 153 or (03) 9032 3583 (9am–5pm Monday to Friday)

Phone (general): 1300 891 848

Website: Victorian Equal Opportunity and Human Rights Commission

·         WorkSafe

Phone: 9641 1444 or 1800 136 089 (toll free)

·         Fair Work Australia

Phone: 1300 799 675 (toll free)

Complaints Procedure

Managers must ensure everyone is treated fairly and are not subject to any form of harassment and must treat reports of possible harassment seriously and sympathetically and investigate reports thoroughly. They must also ensure that no one is disadvantaged or victimised as a result of a harassment complaint being made or investigated.

All complaints are to be addressed with speed, sensitivity, confidentiality, professionalism and consistency. Once all the information has been gathered and all parties have been consulted, the relevant manager, team leader and program manager will make a collective decision on whether, on the balance of probabilities, the complaint is sustained.

Irrespective of the findings of the investigation, the decision will be communicated to all relevant parties, together with an appropriate explanation.

If the complaint is found to have been vexatious, appropriate action may be taken, including counselling, a written apology to the person complained about or disciplinary action, dependent on the seriousness of the allegations.

Workplace bullying is regarded as a serious breach of conduct and will result in an investigation which if proven, may result in disciplinary action being taken against the perpetrator, which may include dismissal.

Bagwan Health will offer staff an opportunity for debriefing after an incident.

Policy and Procedure Code of Conduct

Version Number 001

Scope and purpose

The Bagwan Health Code of Conduct defines standards of ethical and professional conduct that is required of everyone working at Bagwan Health in any capacity. This policy applies to all employees, volunteers and students on placement.

The Code of Conduct sets the standards expected of employees and complies with the relevant legislation, policies and procedures. This policy assists with building a positive workplace culture based on our core Bagwan Health values of compassion, excellence, integrity, unity and respect.

The intent of the Code of Conduct is to provide a framework to promote ethical day-to-day conduct and decision-making. This policy does not address all possible situations that may arise in employment with Bagwan Health but is a set of principles that can provide guidance to employees on acceptable and unacceptable behaviour.

Contents

Terms and definitions

An authorised person is the relevant Manager or the Chief Executive Officer.

Employee is a Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student on placement with Bagwan Health.

A service user is a child or an adult (person with a disability) or aged person who uses a Bagwan Health service.

Company is the reference to the Bagwan Health organisation.

Bagwan Health is the reference to the relevant public health organisations and all other organisations under the control and direction of the Minister for Health or the Secretary of Health.

Code of Conduct

Promote a positive work environment

Observe the human rights of all service users, service users’ families, fellow employees and the public with courtesy and respect and with due sensitivity to the needs of people with different backgrounds and cultures

Treat all Employees (irrespective of whether they are at the same level of seniority, or more senior or junior) in a way that promotes harmonious and productive working relationships, and a collaborative teamwork approach

Behave in a non-discriminatory and non-judgmental manner to their fellow employees, service users, service users’ families, and the public. Do not discriminate against others based on their sex, race, ethnic or ethno-religious background, marital status, pregnancy, disability, age, homosexuality, transgender or carers' responsibilities

Do not participate, encourage or support other Employees in harassing or bullying, or in acting in a way that is contrary to harmonious working relationships between Employees

Where appropriate, attempt to settle any complaints, disagreements or grievances involving other Employees themselves in the first instance; or pursue such matters through their manager or a more senior Employee in a way which is proportionate to the issues raised. Use applicable Bagwan Health policies, that recognises the relevant process to resolve such matters, and respects that other Employees also have perspectives and rights.

Professional and ethical behaviour

Act in a way which is consistent with Bagwan Health’s duties of care to its patients and clients, and its obligations to provide a safe and supportive environment on its premises for patients and their family members

Not be under the influence of alcohol or drugs when commencing work and while at work

Be in a fit and proper condition to carry out their duties when commencing work and while at work

Dress in a way that is appropriate for the work they do, and complies with any local dress requirements

Carry out their duties diligently and efficiently. Ensuring to provide a person-centred approach keeping service users’ and their families’ interests and needs in mind.

Do not absent themselves from the workplace without proper notification, when they are meant to be on duty; nor engage in any form of outside practice or employment or other activities when they are meant to be on duty and working for Bagwan Health

Comply with all lawful and reasonable directions given by their managers or other members of staff authorised to give them Bagwan Health agency where they work

Maintain and enhance their professional standards and skills and keep up to date with best practice. As well as participate in any mandatory training/information/supervision sessions as required by Bagwan Health.

Observe all laws, professional codes of conduct and ethics relating to their profession

If professionally registered, report all changes in professional registration (such as the imposition of conditions on registration) to their manager

Act in a way which protects and promotes the interests of Bagwan Health and the Bagwan Health agency where they work

Avoid conduct that could bring Bagwan Health or any of its employees, patients or clients into disrepute, including when using social media

Only provide official comment on matters related to Bagwan Health if authorised to do so

When making public comment on issues or participating in political or industrial activities, not indicate or imply that their views are those of Bagwan Health

Notify Bagwan Health if they are charged with a criminal offence or any offence that affects their capacity to perform their duties, (including the validity of their driver’s license)

Report criminal charges and convictions against them involving offences punishable by imprisonment for 12 months or more to their Chief Executive within 7 days of the charge being laid or a conviction recorded

Report to the designated person within their Health organisation, upon becoming aware of an allegation, charge or conviction involving an under 18-year-old against another Bagwan Health employee member

Report immediately any episode or incident of clinical care which raises concerns about standards of clinical care or about possible clinical malpractice

Report to a more senior member and/or to the appropriate external statutory body any misconduct by others of which they become aware, such as corruption, fraud, maladministration, and serious or substantial waste.

Conflict of interest

Employees must take reasonable steps to avoid any actual or potential conflict of interest and act in the best interests of Bagwan Health including, but not limited to, by:

Perform duties primarily in the interests of the Bagwan Health’s strategic direction and mission to deliver world-leading care and services to our patients

Avoid situations which may give rise to financial or other conflicts of interest. Should any conflicts or possible perceptions of such conflicts arise, declare them immediately to their manager

Disclose actual or potential conflict of interest and withdraw themselves immediately from the situation giving rise to the conflict

Ensure that their actions and decisions are not influenced by self-interest or considerations of personal gain or other improper motives

Do not misuse the influence of their position to pursue personal, sexual or financial relationships with other Employees, service users, service users’ families or members of the community and public

Do not accept bribes or inducements that are intended to influence their decisions or actions

Do not accept gifts which go beyond common courtesies consistent with ethical and accepted business practices and/or can be reasonably interpreted as being designed to secure influence in favour of the giver. Token or inexpensive gifts offered as an expression of gratitude, such as chocolates from a patient, can be accepted

Provide honest and accurate comments when giving Employees reference

Observe confidentiality concerning the agency or its service users regarding any information gained during their employment.

Do not take documents that are the property of the health services or Bagwan Health to another position prior to or after resignation without approval.

Use of company resources

Employees are expected to use all Company facilities, equipment and processes efficiently, carefully and in a proper manner by:

Using Bagwan Health resources efficiently and economically. Making sure to secure resources against theft, damage, or misuse

Pursue the principles of sustainability and understanding the impacts and opportunities of their work in the workplace

Use all equipment, goods, resources and materials provided for work-related purposes only, and not for outside clinical or business practice or political purposes

Do not use Bagwan Health internet and email resources for accessing, transmitting, storing or downloading pornographic, sexually explicit or otherwise inappropriate material

Maintain the security of confidential and/or sensitive official information.

Keep all personal information and records confidential, including not discussing or providing information on social media that could identify patients or divulge patient information

Do not use or release official information or records without proper authority

Maintain the security of confidential and/or sensitive information, including that

stored on communication devices

Do not disclose, use or take advantage of information obtained during official

duties, including when they cease to work in Bagwan Health.

Roles and responsibilities

All employees are responsible for applying and complying with the Code of Conduct. Managers are responsible for ensuring that the Employees who they supervise are aware of and understand their responsibilities under the Code of Conduct.

Bagwan Health is responsible for developing, adopting and reviewing this policy.

Bagwan Health’s CEO is responsible for the implementation of this policy, for monitoring changes in related legislation, and for advising on the need to review or revise this policy as and when the need arises.

Reporting a breach in Code of Conduct

Employees should report any breach or concerns about a breach of the Code of Conduct to their manager.

If Employees are not comfortable about reporting to their manager, they should report the matter to a more senior Employees member. In some circumstances, such as allegations of corruption, there is a mandatory requirement to report matters to external agencies.

Bagwan Health is committed to protecting any person who raises concerns about a breach of the Code of Conduct from retaliation or reprisals.

Any attempt to take detrimental action against a person who raises a legitimate breach of the Code of Conduct will be treated seriously and may lead to disciplinary action.

It is a criminal offence to take reprisal against a whistleblower under Public Interest Disclosures Act 1994 where a disclosure falls within the scope of that Act.

What happens if there is a breach in Code of Conduct

There is a range of consequences for breaches of this Code of Conduct depending on the nature and seriousness of the matter.

Managers have a responsibility to address alleged breaches of the Code of Conduct promptly, and in a fair and reasonable manner. They need to assess the seriousness of any alleged breaches, and how they should be dealt with.

Possible outcomes for an Employee who has breached the Code of Conduct may be:

Counselling

Performance improvement plans

Formal disciplinary action

Referral to the relevant registration board when the Employees member is a registered health practitioner

Referral to the police in cases of suspected possible criminal activity

Referral to other Government agencies, such as the Independent Commission Against Corruption

Termination of employment

Certain sections of the Code of Conduct reflect the requirements of legislation, and breaches of these conditions may be punishable under law.

This policy applies to all employees, volunteers and students on placement. The Code of Conduct sets the standards expected of employees and complies with the relevant legislation, policies and procedures. This policy assists with building a positive workplace culture based on our core Bagwan Health values of compassion, excellence, integrity, unity and respect. The intent of the Code of Conduct is to provide a framework to promote ethical day-to-day conduct and decision-making. This policy does not address all possible situations that may arise in employment with Bagwan Health but is a set of principles that can provide guidance to employees on acceptable and unacceptable behaviour. Contents Terms and definitions An authorised person is the relevant Manager or the Chief Executive Officer. Employee is a Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student on placement with Bagwan Health. A service user is a child or an adult (person with a disability) or aged person who uses a Bagwan Health service. Company is the reference to the Bagwan Health organisation. Bagwan Health is the reference to the relevant public health organisations and all other organisations under the control and direction of the Minister for Health or the Secretary of Health. Code of Conduct Promote a positive work environment Observe the human rights of all service users, service users’ families, fellow employees and the public with courtesy and respect and with due sensitivity to the needs of people with different backgrounds and cultures Treat all Employees (irrespective of whether they are at the same level of seniority, or more senior or junior) in a way that promotes harmonious and productive working relationships, and a collaborative teamwork approach Behave in a non-discriminatory and non-judgmental manner to their fellow employees, service users, service users’ families, and the public. Do not discriminate against others based on their sex, race, ethnic or ethno-religious background, marital status, pregnancy, disability, age, homosexuality, transgender or carers' responsibilities Do not participate, encourage or support other Employees in harassing or bullying, or in acting in a way that is contrary to harmonious working relationships between Employees Where appropriate, attempt to settle any complaints, disagreements or grievances involving other Employees themselves in the first instance; or pursue such matters through their manager or a more senior Employee in a way which is proportionate to the issues raised. Use applicable Bagwan Health policies, that recognises the relevant process to resolve such matters, and respects that other Employees also have perspectives and rights. Professional and ethical behaviour Act in a way which is consistent with Bagwan Health’s duties of care to its patients and clients, and its obligations to provide a safe and supportive environment on its premises for patients and their family members Not be under the influence of alcohol or drugs when commencing work and while at work Be in a fit and proper condition to carry out their duties when commencing work and while at work Dress in a way that is appropriate for the work they do, and complies with any local dress requirements Carry out their duties diligently and efficiently. Ensuring to provide a person-centred approach keeping service users’ and their families’ interests and needs in mind. Do not absent themselves from the workplace without proper notification, when they are meant to be on duty; nor engage in any form of outside practice or employment or other activities when they are meant to be on duty and working for Bagwan Health Comply with all lawful and reasonable directions given by their managers or other members of staff authorised to give them Bagwan Health agency where they work Maintain and enhance their professional standards and skills and keep up to date with best practice. pages.title: Complaints and feedback handling
pages.html:
Policy Number

Version Number

Scope

This policy applies to all staff (paid and volunteer), contractors and our governing body, receiving or managing complaints from the public and clients made to or about Bagwan Health regarding products, services and staff, or the complaint handling process.

Policy statement

Bagwan Health respects the rights of patients and their families and encourages them to promptly bring concerns or complaints to our attention so that they can be addressed in a timely fashion. Every complaint is an opportunity to improve the quality of our service. This policy defines the standards and processes associated with complaints handling to ensure that Bagwan Health handles complaints fairly, efficiently and effectively.

What is a Complaint?

A “complaint” is an expression of dissatisfaction made to or about us, our services, staff or the handling of a complaint where a response or resolution is explicitly or implicitly expected or legally required. (AS/NZ 10002:2014)

Commitment to Complaints Handling

Bagwan Health is committed to seeking and receiving feedback and complaints about our services, systems, practices, procedures, products and complaint handling. Any concerns raised will be dealt with within a reasonable time frame. (AS/NZ 10002)

  Responsibilities

Bagwan Health staff at all levels are expected to be fair, effective and efficient when handling complaints. The responsibilities will vary depending on their level of involvement in complaint handling.

The CEO of Bagwan Health is responsible for:

  • Reporting to the governing body on complaint handling.
  • Providing adequate support and direction to key staff responsible for handling complaints
  • Regularly reviewing reports about complaint trends and issues arising from complaints
  • Encouraging staff to be alert to complaints and assisting those responsible for handling complaints to resolve them promptly
  • Encouraging staff to make recommendations for system improvements
  • Supporting recommendations for service, staff and complaint handling improvements arising from the analysis of complaint data

Bagwan Health staff whose duties include complaint handling are responsible for:

  • Treating all people with respect, including people who make complaints
  • Assisting people to make a complaint, if needed
  • Complying with our complaints handling policy and associated procedures
  • Providing regular feedback to management and/or the governing body on issues arising from complaints
  • Providing suggestions to management on ways to improve our complaints handling system
  • Implementing changes arising from individual complaints and from the analysis of complaint data as directed by management

All Bagwan Health staff are responsible for:

  • Treating all people with respect, including people who make complaints
  • Being aware of our complaint handling policies and procedures
  • Assisting people who wish to make complaints access our complaints process
  • Being aware of complaints and assisting staff handling complaints to promptly resolve matters

  Empowerment of Staff

Bagwan Health staff are empowered to resolve complaints promptly and to implement the complaint handling system as relevant to their role and responsibilities. Complaints handling is an important component of Bagwan Health orientation and quality training programs. As such all Bagwan Health staff must be familiar with the process.

Accessibility

Information on how and where to make complaints can be found on the Bagwan Health website. The systems used to manage complaints are easily understood and accessible to everyone, particularly people who may require assistance.

Information on complaints management can also be found in:

  • Patient admission information
  • Patient booklet
  • Signage throughout Bagwan Health
  • Patient feedback forms

Compliant forms are offered to patients in all areas of Bagwan Health including reception desks, waiting rooms and on the Bagwan Health website (Contact Us tab).

Objectivity and Fairness

Complaints will be addressed with integrity and in an equitable, objective and unbiased manner. The person handling a complaint will be different from any staff member whose conduct or service is being complained about. Conflicts of interest, whether actual or perceived, will be managed responsibly. In particular, internal reviews of how a complaint was managed will be conducted by a person other than the original decision maker.

At all times throughout this process independent advocacy will be offered to the complainant as an option for resolution. An independent advocacy service may be chosen or an appropriate support person contacted from the details enclosed in the Bagwan Health Complaints Handling pamphlet which is given/sent on first contact.

When a complainant prefers or needs another person or organisation to assist or represent them in the making and/or resolution of their complaint, Bagwan Health staff will communicate with them through their representative. Anyone may represent a person wishing to make a complaint with their consent.

Complainants with special needs must be recognized and appropriate support put in place to support them with the complaint process e.g. access to an interpreter.  

Confidentiality

Bagwan Health will take all reasonable steps to ensure that people making complaints are not adversely affected because a complaint has been made by them or on their behalf.

Where practical, the identity of the complainants will be protected. Personal information that identifies individuals will only be disclosed or used by Bagwan Health as permitted under the relevant privacy laws, secrecy provisions and relevant confidentiality obligations.

No Charge

There is no charging for making a complaint.

Types of Complaints

Complaints come in many forms and staff must follow the process for receiving, documenting, escalating and resolving complaints whether they are verbal or written, formal or informal. As well as complaints being made directly to our organisation, some complaints (e.g. negative comments) can be made on social media. Where possible, complaints will be resolved on first contact.

Verbal Complaints

When a verbal complaint is received by a member of staff it will be acknowledged immediately and if it is able to be resolved, all attempts will be made to do so at the time. If this is not appropriate the staff member receiving the complaint must document the complaint and escalate it to their Manager who will risk score the complaint and decide whether further action should be taken (refer to Appendix One).

The Manager will pass the complaint to the Administration Assistant to ensure it is documented on the Complaints Register.

Written Complaints

When a written complaint is received, it must be promptly forwarded to the Administration Assistant or Executive Assistant, who notify the appropriate Executive/Manager to risk score the complaint and decide on an appropriate response. (Refer to Appendix One). The Administration Assistant will ensure it is documented on the Complaints Register.

Complaints received by any staff member other than Reception staff must also be discussed with the appropriate Manager as soon as possible.

  Staff Performance Issues

If a staff performance issue is implicated in either a verbal or written complaint, the complaint will be passed onto the appropriate Manager. The Manager will follow up with the staff member concerned. If necessary, the Manager will refer the complaint to the People and Capability Manager who will ensure that the appropriate performance management process is followed.

Complaints Involving Multiple Organisations

Where a complaint involves multiple organisations, Bagwan Health will work with the other organisation/s to ensure that communication with the complainant and/or their representative is clear and coordinated. Subject to privacy and confidentiality considerations, communication and information sharing between the parties will also be organised to facilitate a timely response to the complaint.

Bagwan Health takes complaints not only about the actions of our staff but also the actions of our service providers. Where our services are contracted out, we expect contracted service providers to have an accessible and comprehensive complaint handling system.

Complaints Register

For tracking purposes a unique identifier/number will be assigned to every complaint recorded in the Complaints Register.

The complaint file will include:

  • Contact information for the person making a complaint
  • The date the complaint was received
  • Issues raised by the complainant and the desired outcome/s
  • Any other relevant information
  • Any additional support that the person making the complaint requires

Acknowledgment

The receipt of a complaint will be acknowledged promptly and preferably within two working days. When appropriate an explanation or apology may be offered. Consideration will also be given to the most appropriate medium (e.g. email, letter) for communicating with the person making a complaint.

 

To manage expectations, complainants will be informed soon as possible of the following:

  • The complaints process and the expected time frames for Bagwan Health
  • Their likely involvement in the complaint handling process
  • The progress of the complaint
  • When expected time frames cannot be met and the reason for the delay
  • When Bagwan Health is unable to deal with any part of their complaint and where such issues/complaints should be directed (if known or appropriate)
  • The possible or likely outcome of their complain

Initial Assessment of the Complaint

Once the receipt of the complaint is acknowledged, Bagwan Health staff will confirm whether the issue/s raised in the complaint is/are within our control. The outcome/s sought by the complainant will also be considered and, where there is more than one issue raised, it will be determined whether each issue needs to be separately addressed.

When determining how a complaint will be managed, the following will be taken into consideration:

  • How serious, complicated or urgent the complaint is
  • Whether the complaint raises concerns about people’s health and safety
  • How the person making the complaint is being affected
  • The risks involved if resolution of the complaint is delayed
  • Whether a resolution requires the involvement of other organisations

Complaints will be assessed and prioritised in accordance with the urgency and/or seriousness of the issues raised. If a matter concerns an immediate risk to safety or security then the response will be immediate and will be escalated appropriately.

Investigating the Complaint

Once the complaint has been assessed, it will be decided how the complaint will be managed. This may be done by:

  • Giving the complainant an explanation
  • Gathering information about the issue, person or area that the complaint is about
  • Investigating the claims made in the complaint

The complainant will continue to be kept up-to-date on the complaint progress, especially if there are any delays.  

Determining Outcomes and Actions

Once the complaint has been investigated, a decision on the outcome of the complaint and any required actions will be determined. Outcomes and determined actions must be tailored to each case and take into account any statutory requirements. The staff member dealing with the complaint will then:

  • Ensure the Complaints Register has been updated
  • Notify the Executive/Manager of actions if they are not dealing with the complaint
  • If actions are appropriate and no further action is required, the complainant will receive a written response within ten working days, from the decision date
  • If actions require more work, the complainant will be advised of this along with the expected timeframe
  • This cycle will be repeated and the Complaints Register will be updated until actions are sufficient to resolve the complaint
  • If time frames are likely to be greater than 20 days, the complainant will be informed of the progress of the complaint and the reasons for any delay by the person undertaking action

Providing Reasons for Decision

The staff member dealing the complaint will contact the person making the complaint and advise them:

  • The outcome of the complaint and any action taken
  • The reason/s for the decision
  • The remedy or resolution/s that have been proposed or put in place
  • Any options for review that may be available to the complainant, such as an internal review, external review or appeal

Note: Staff must inform complainants of any internal or external review options available to them including any relevant Ombudsman or oversight regulatory bodies. Closing the Complaint

Bagwan Health will ensure that outcomes and actions are properly implemented, monitored and reported to the complaint handling Manager, Senior Management, the CEO and the Board. Bagwan Health will keep records about the complaint, including:

  • How the complaint was managed
  • The outcome/s of the complaint
  • Any outstanding actions to be followed up

  Continuous Improvement

Bagwan Health is committed to improving the way our organisation operates, including our management of the effectiveness and efficiency of our complaint handling system.

Complaints are recorded in a systematic way so that information can be easily retrieved for reporting by management and the Board.

Regular reports are run on:

  • Number of complaints received
  • Outcome of complaints
  • Issues arising from complaints
  • Identified systemic issues
  • Number of requests received for review of our complaint handling

Regular analysis of these reports will be undertaken to monitor trends, measure the quality of our customer service and make improvements. Both reporting and their analysis will be provided, at least annually, to the CEO, Senior Management and to the Board for review.

These reports will also be used as key performance indicators.

pages.title: Emergency response
pages.html:
Policy Name – Emergency Response

Scope

This policy applies to all staff and contractors employed by Bagwan Health, Allied Health professionals, Credentialed Specialists, students, volunteers, patients and visitors.

Policy

Bagwan Health is committed to the provision of high quality services to patients and their families and to minimising risks to patients and their families, staff, contractors, volunteers, students, and members of the community. This commitment encompasses both proactive Risk Management and Incident Reporting and subsequent analysis to inform continuous service improvement.

In line with incident reporting guidelines, Bagwan Health is also required to complete, keep on file and provide copies of incident reports to funding bodies or other authorities, such as the DHHS, the Commission of Children and Young People, and AHPRA.

This policy provides Bagwan Health staff, contractors, volunteers and students with information to assist them with reporting incidents in a correct and timely manner, and to define the processes for analysing and utilising incident reporting for service improvement.

Procedure 

Code

Action to be taken
Code Red — smoke or fire alert R — remove those in danger
A — activate alarm and call 555
C — confine; shut fire containment doors if these have not automatically closed
E — evacuate/extinguish
    • Stand by for instruction from the area warden (yellow hat or vest), door warden (red hat or vest), emergency officer (white hat or vest) or fire brigade.

  • Do not leave the area unless a Code Orange is called, or the Respond Red is announced as ‘all clear’
Code Orange —evacuation
    • Prepare for evacuation as directed by the area warden (yellow hat or vest), door warden (red hat or vest), emergency officer (white hat or vest) or fire brigade.

    • Advise area warden of your patient’s needs and status as requested.

    • Assist to evacuate and treat patients as instructed. Ambulant patients are evacuated first, followed by patients using wheelchairs, then bed bound patients. Do not block the emergency exits

    • Evacuation will take place horizontally in the first instance. This includes evacuating to the next compartment behind the fire doors, or neighboring wards. Vertical evacuation to other levels of the building occurs next if required, followed by evacuating externally
Code Purple — bomb threat
    • If you become aware of a bomb threat by phone, take note of as many details as you can regarding location, timing and nature of the bomb. Keep the caller on the line while alerting another staff member to call 555 and state “Respond Purple” and the location. Do not hang up the phone even if the caller has ended the call. Report to the nearest senior staff member.

    • If you find a suspicious device or threatening letter, do not touch it and report it to the nearest senior staff member. Move all patients, staff and visitors as far away as possible

    • Stand by for instructions from the area warden (yellow hat or vest), door warden (red hat or vest), emergency officer (white hat or vest) or fire brigade/police.

    • Do not leave the area unless advised to, or the code is announced ‘all clear Respond Purple’.

  • Switch off mobile phones
Code Black — serious aggression/weapon
    • If you are subjected to or become aware of a Code Black incident ensure your own safety by moving away from the violent person. Always ensure that you maintain a path of escape.

    • If safe to do so, dial the emergency number and state “Respond Black” followed by your location

    • Victoria Police will be called to attend by switchboard staff when a Respond Black is called

    • To avoid panic amongst staff, a Code Black is never announced, it will be sent to staff pagers

    • Take no action that will increase the threat.

    • All doors are to be closed and locked. No staff member, patient or visitor will be allowed in or out of locked doors, and the building will assume “lockdown”. This means that any MET calls or Code Blue calls may not be attended to by any staff from external areas.

    • Staff, patients and visitors are to move away from windows and close any window blinds

    • Stand by for instructions from the area warden (yellow hat or vest), door warden (red hat or vest), emergency officer (white hat or vest) or member of the police

    • When the threat has been appropriately managed, an ‘all clear’ Respond Black”will be sent to all staff pagers

  • Staff involved in the Code Black will attend a mandatory debriefing
Code Grey — threatening behaviour
    • If you are subjected to or become aware of a Code Grey incident ensure your own safety by moving away from the violent patient. Always ensure that you maintain a path of escape.

    • Dial the emergency number and state “Respond Grey” followed by your exact location.

    • A senior clinician will take charge of the response.

    • Continue listening and talking to the patient to defuse the situation.

    • Take instructions from the senior clinician in charge of the Code Grey response. Security staff will attend and take instruction from the Nurse in Charge of the ward

    • Do not leave the area unless advised to or the code is declared ‘all clear’.

  • Assist staff to manage patients as guided and directed by clinical staff of the area.
Code Blue — medical emergency
    • If you become aware of a medical emergency dial the emergency number and state “Respond Blue” followed by your location, the patient bed number and treating medical team. Alternatively, pressing the red ‘Emergency’ button in the patient rooms will sound an alarm throughout the ward, and automatically alert switchboard to announce the location of the Respond Blue

    • A senior clinician will take charge of the Code Blue emergency response team.

    • Take instructions from the senior clinician in charge of the Code Blue response.

    • Determine the patients resuscitation status, and if for resuscitation, commence CPR and await staff from the Coronary Cary Unit and Intensive Care Unit to arrive and assist with patient resuscitation. All available nursing and medical staff on the ward should attend and leave if not required

    • Assist staff to manage patient as guided and directed by clinical staff of the area.

  • Staff involved in the Code Blue will be offered a debriefing following the event
Code Yellow — internal emergency
    • If you discover an internal emergency (e.g. flood, noxious fumes), call the emergency number and state “Respond Yellow” followed by the exact location and nature of the emergency.

  • Stand by for instructions from the area warden (yellow hat or vest), door warden (red hat or vest), emergency officer (white hat or vest) or fire brigade/police.
Code Brown — external emergency
    • If you become aware of an external emergency that will impact the facility call the emergency number and state “Respond Brown” followed by the nature of the emergency.

    • Stand by for instructions from the area warden (yellow hat or vest), door warden (red hat or vest), emergency officer (white hat or vest) or fire brigade/police.

  • Staff in the Emergency Department in conjunction with the Site Manager will contact additional staff to come into the hospital to manage the extra patient load that is expected from an external emergency

 

Incident Response and Reporting Principles

The following principles apply to all incidents at Bagwan Health.

1. People first

Respond to the incident and with the people involved first. Your priority is to ensure the risk and impact to people (including yourself) is minimised as quickly as possible. Notify your supervisor as soon as practical or if you need to clarify anything. Always ask for help if required.

2. Report all incidents

Complete the reports required including a complete, sequential, factual and clearly written account of the events. If in doubt about if an incident should be reported, report it.

3. Submit reports to the right place

Submit all reports to the appropriate location.

Procedures for Responding any Incident Involving a Patient 

Once you are aware of an incident that impacts a patient (in progress or afterwards), they must immediately:

1. Protect the patient from further harm. Failure to respond and protect the patient from further harm following an incident is a breach of duty of care and can lead to disciplinary action.

2. Administer first aid a patient that has been seriously injured and warrants urgent medical review, call a MET (Medical Emergency Team) call via the emergency number 555.

When to call Victoria Police immediately

The Victoria Police Service must be called by dialling 000 if:

  • The incident is serious or life-threatening and
  • There is a threat of danger to people or property
  • It is a serious crime (e.g. physical or sexual assault)

It is a situation that requires Victoria Police Service assistance

For all other cases
Contact the team leader or manager to authorise calling the Victoria Police Service.

 

3. For suspected, observed, or alleged abuse and neglect of patient incidents, follow the response requirements detailed in the Mandatory Reporting policy.

4. Protect any evidence. If necessary, secure the scene of the incident for internal and/or external investigation.

5. Contact the team leader or manager. For serious incidents, contact must be made within the first 30 minutes. 

6. Complete a Bagwan Health – Incident Report or enter incident details in the digital Bagwan Health Incident Reporting Information System. This reporting must be done within two hours of the incident by the staff            member who first identified the incident.

The Bagwan Health – Incident Report must be completed, scanned, and emailed to your direct supervisor and the Bagwan Health Administration Department (admin@bgh.gov.au). Upon receiving the report, the Administration Department must enter the details from the report into the IRIS by the end of the next business day. Your direct supervisor may follow up with up as well.

 

 

Additional Steps for Serious Incidents Involving a Patient

 

For serious incidents, you must:

 

7. Contact the team leader or manager. Once the patient has been protected from further harm, necessary first aid administered, and if required, emergency services contacted, the staff member who was first aware of the serious incident must make a verbal report to the team leader or manager within the initial 30mins.

8. It is important that the report is done in person or over the phone, with the team leader or manager providing verbal confirmation that they have been informed. 

9. DO NOT leave written or verbal messages. Only staff who are unable to communicate verbally (i.e., are Deaf or have a hearing impairment) can send a text message. Enough information must be provided in the text message so that the incident is fully understood. The team leader or manager must follow-up with an in-person meeting as soon as possible to ensure the requirements of this procedure are properly carried out.

10. If the staff member reporting the incident is unable to contact and speak with the team leader or manager, they must phone the service manager. If the service manager cannot be reached, then they must contact the General Manager.

11. Carry out follow-up actions as directed by the team leader or manager. This can include contacting the patient’s emergency contact to inform them of the incident.

 

 

Responsibilities

 

Every incident must be reported. An incident report (Bagwan Health – Incident Report) must be completed by the staff member who witnessed the incident. If there were no witnesses, it must be completed by the staff member who was first on scene after the incident occurred, or the staff member whom the incident was reported to. There are specific responsibilities depending on your role within Bagwan Health.

 

General Responsibilities

 

All staff, contractors, volunteers and students are required to: 

 

• Have read this policy and procedures

• Whenever an incident occurs staff need to apply the Incident Response & Reporting Principles and follow the Procedure for Responding to any Incident Involving a Patient 

• After the immediate emergency has passed, complete the relevant electronic/online incident report(s) – see the section Reporting Incidents at Bagwan Health of this document for reports that must be actioned.

• Consult with the relevant team leader or manager available regarding next steps and any information they require.

• Inform the patient’s family of incidents that involve injury or hospitalisation of their relative, according to agreed arrangements and of all allegations of physical and/or sexual assault.

• Complete any other reports required such as the DINMA report, patient progress or case notes, etc.

 

Incident categorisation rule

Staff, contractors, Allied Health professionals, Credentialed Specialists and students who are unsure of the category of an incident, should treat the report as being at the higher level or check with their supervisor as soon as possible.


Team Leader and Manager Responsibilities

Team Leaders and Managers are responsible for ensuring that:

·         An online incident report has been completed.

·         Reporting processes have been followed within required timelines.

·         All other required reports – as per this policy and or regulatory requirements – are completed and forwarded to the appropriate government or regulatory body.

·         The patient’s family is informed of incidents that involve injury or hospitalisation of their relative, according to agreed arrangements and of all allegations of physical and/or sexual assault.

·         Ensure patients are offered medical assistance and counselling as required.

·         Communication strategies have been followed to ensure all relevant hospital staff, contractors, volunteers and students are aware of the incident and any recommendations or control measures that may prevent or reduce the risk of the incident reoccurring.

·         Analysis of incident trends and implementation of recommendations and or control measures is documented. 

·         Reporting to the Board any CIMS Major and Non-Major incidents and incidents reported on the Bagwan Health Incident Reporting Tool at the next scheduled meeting or immediately if there are serious immediate implications for the organisation

·         The Manager (Division) or CEO to report to DHHS Major incidents (DHHS and NDIS funded services) within 24 hrs. to DHHS

·         Investigate and assess each incident and develop control measures and risk management plans accordingly. This can be done by using the online CIMS tools in case of an incident impacting on patients (DHHS and NDIS funded services).

·         Analyse the events to add any relevant information to Occupational Violence Risk Assessments or Client Behaviour Support Plans

 

·         Ensure Incident Report findings and recommendations are recorded for Continuous Improvement towards Risk Management, OH&S and Quality systems.

Bagwan Health CEO Responsibilities

The Bagwan Health Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is accountable for all incidents at or related to Bagwan Health and is responsible for ensuring:

·         Continuous improvement strategies are development and implemented

 

·         Internal and external reporting requirements are met, in line with relevant legislated requirements.

All incident reports – both internal to Bagwan Health and external reports to government or regulatory bodies – must include a complete, sequential, factual and account of the events.

Reporting Child Abuse and Neglect Incidents

The Victorian Reportable Conduct Scheme requires the centralised reporting of allegations of child abuse (sexual, physical and psychological) from workers or volunteers in relevant organisations with a high level of responsibility for children. From 1 January 2018 the scheme was applied to hospitals, other disability services for children, providers of overnight camps, religious bodies and the residential facilities of boarding schools.

The Victorian Reportable Conduct Scheme requires allegations of suspected criminal conduct to be reported to Victoria Police as the first priority and will maintain the primacy of an investigation by Victoria Police of any allegations of criminal misconduct.

For child abuse and neglect incidents the On-Call Management or Division Manager and CEO need to be informed immediately. Bagwan Health CEO (or her delegate) must report any allegation of reportable conduct to the Commission for Children and Young People within three business days of becoming aware of the allegation. It is a criminal offence for Bagwan Health CEO to fail to notify (within 3 business days) and update (within 30 calendar days) the Commission for Children and Young People (CCYP) about reportable allegations.

Bagwan Health CEO Responsibilities

The Bagwan Health CEO needs to be informed immediately of any child abuse or neglect incidents. The CEO (or a delegate) must report any allegation of reportable conduct to the Commission for Children and Young People (CCYP) within 3 business days of becoming aware of the allegation. It is a criminal offence for Bagwan Health CEO to fail to notify (within 3 business days) and update (within 30 calendar days) the CCYP about reportable allegations.

The reporting to the CCYP by the Bagwan Health CEO is in addition to all the current steps that are required to be undertaken when an allegation of child abuse (sexual, physical and psychological) or significant neglect is made.

Emergency Response Procedures

Bagwan Health is committed to ensuring a safe environment and appropriate emergency preparedness for our visiting doctors. To help us achieve this you are required to: 

• Take responsibility for working safely by complying with safety procedures and not harming others by your actions or omissions

• Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) where required

• Use safety equipment provided 

• Raise any safety concerns you may have

• In an emergency follow instructions from the person in charge. 

In the event of an internal emergency the person in charge has legal authority to direct all parties. Initially the person in charge will be the area warden who will be identified by a yellow hat or vest. Once the emergency officer arrives on the scene they will support the area warden. The emergency officer is identified by a white hat or vest.

Everybody on the site, no matter how senior, is legally required to follow the directions of the area warden or emergency officer — therefore, the primary role of the specialist in an internal emergency is to follow the instructions of those in charge.

Evacuation

If you are requested to assist in the evacuation of patients, please note that the order of evacuation is as follows:

• Ambulant patients and visitors first

• Semi-ambulant next

• Non-ambulant last.

When directed to evacuate an area, you should do so immediately. If gathering personal items, do so promptly and do not endanger yourself in doing this. 

Lifts should not be used during a Code Red incident unless approved by the fire brigade. 

If evacuation is required, a Code Orange will be called. In normal circumstances, the area warden will coordinate this.

The Role of the Specialist during an Internal Emergency in the Operating Theatres

The role of the specialist in theatres is potentially more complex than on the wards. Primarily the specialist’s responsibility during an internal emergency in theatre is to ready the patient for evacuation as quickly and safely as possible.

The specialist is still expected to take direction from the area warden or emergency officer, however this direction will require critical medical input in determining when and how to safely move patients. 

Evacuation Diagrams

Each area has wall-mounted evacuation diagrams indicating the location of key fire safety features including:

• Break glass alarms

• Hose reels

• Fire extinguishers

• Exit points

• WIPs — warden intercommunication phone

• Assembly areas.

You should note the location and information contained on these diagrams when working in an area.

The internal Emergency number extension is 555. This extension is used for notifying emergencies and will be given priority by switchboard staff/person answering the call.
