Procedure for responding to any incident involving a patient Child abuse and neglect incidents Report to the Commission for Children Bagwan Health CEO Reporting child abuse and neglect incidents Incidents that seriously impact staff, contractor, volunteer or student Worksafe VIC – Incident notification form Any staff, contractor, volunteer or student that is involved in and/or witnesses the incident occur or attends soon after the incident. Refer to Occupational Health and Safety policy Suspected crimes Verbal report maybe required Any staff, contractor, volunteer or student that is involved in and/or witnesses the incident occur or attends soon after the incident. Procedure for responding to any incident involving a patient Reporting Child Abuse and Neglect Incidents The Victorian Reportable Conduct Scheme requires the centralised reporting of allegations of child abuse (sexual, physical and psychological) from workers or volunteers in relevant organisations with a high level of responsibility for children. From 1 January 2018 the scheme was applied to hospitals, other disability services for children, providers of overnight camps, religious bodies and the residential facilities of boarding schools. The Victorian Reportable Conduct Scheme requires allegations of suspected criminal conduct to be reported to Victoria Police as the first priority and will maintain the primacy of an investigation by Victoria Police of any allegations of criminal misconduct. For child abuse and neglect incidents the On-Call Management or Division Manager and CEO need to be informed immediately. Bagwan Health CEO (or her delegate) must report any allegation of reportable conduct to the Commission for Children and Young People within three business days of becoming aware of the allegation. It is a criminal offence for Bagwan Health CEO to fail to notify (within 3 business days) and update (within 30 calendar days) the Commission for Children and Young People (CCYP) about reportable allegations. Bagwan Health CEO Responsibilities The Bagwan Health CEO needs to be informed immediately of any child abuse or neglect incidents. The CEO (or a delegate) must report any allegation of reportable conduct to the Commission for Children and Young People (CCYP) within 3 business days of becoming aware of the allegation. It is a criminal offence for Bagwan Health CEO to fail to notify (within 3 business days) and update (within 30 calendar days) the CCYP about reportable allegations. The reporting to the CCYP by the Bagwan Health CEO is in addition to all the current steps that are required to be undertaken when an allegation of child abuse (sexual, physical and psychological) or significant neglect is made. Emergency Response Procedures Bagwan Health is committed to ensuring a safe environment and appropriate emergency preparedness for our visiting doctors. To help us achieve this you are required to: • Take responsibility for working safely by complying with safety procedures and not harming others by your actions or omissions • Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) where required • Use safety equipment provided • Raise any safety concerns you may have • In an emergency follow instructions from the person in charge. In the event of an internal emergency the person in charge has legal authority to direct all parties. Initially the person in charge will be the area warden who will be identified by a yellow hat or vest. Once the emergency officer arrives on the scene they will support the area warden. The emergency officer is identified by a white hat or vest. Everybody on the site, no matter how senior, is legally required to follow the directions of the area warden or emergency officer — therefore, the primary role of the specialist in an internal emergency is to follow the instructions of those in charge. Evacuation If you are requested to assist in the evacuation of patients, please note that the order of evacuation is as follows: • Ambulant patients and visitors first • Semi-ambulant next • Non-ambulant last. When directed to evacuate an area, you should do so immediately. If gathering personal items, do so promptly and do not endanger yourself in doing this. Lifts should not be used during a Code Red incident unless approved by the fire brigade. If evacuation is required, a Code Orange will be called. In normal circumstances, the area warden will coordinate this. The Role of the Specialist during an Internal Emergency in the Operating Theatres The role of the specialist in theatres is potentially more complex than on the wards. Primarily the specialist’s responsibility during an internal emergency in theatre is to ready the patient for evacuation as quickly and safely as possible. The specialist is still expected to take direction from the area warden or emergency officer, however this direction will require critical medical input in determining when and how to safely move patients. Evacuation Diagrams Each area has wall-mounted evacuation diagrams indicating the location of key fire safety features including: • Break glass alarms • Hose reels • Fire extinguishers • Exit points • WIPs — warden intercommunication phone • Assembly areas. You should note the location and information contained on these diagrams when working in an area. The internal Emergency number extension is 555. This extension is used for notifying emergencies and will be given priority by switchboard staff/person answering the call. Click here to download policies

Policy and Procedure Equal Opportunity and Anti-discrimination 

 

 

Scope and purpose

 

Bagwan Health seeks to promote gender equality, a working environment that is free of discrimination, and one that ensures every employee or potential employee has equal employment opportunities.

 

This policy has been developed to communicate Bagwan Health’ commitment to achieving equal employment opportunities for all employees and potential employees, whilst recognising the true potential of each employee as a means of increasing the effectiveness of the organisation.

  

Terms and definitions

 

An authorised person is the relevant Manager or the Chief Executive Officer.

 

An employee is a Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student on placement with Bagwan Health.

 

Individual refers to Bagwan Health service users, families and friends, employees, potential employees, volunteers, students and the community.

 

A service user is a child or an adult (person with a disability) or aged person who uses a Bagwan Health service.

 

Workplace includes working on-site or off-site, attendance at a work-related conference or function, and attendance at a client or other work-related event, including retreats and social events.

 

Discrimination is when a person or group is treated less favourably than another person or group in a similar situation because of a personal characteristic protected by law. Indirectly, when an unreasonable requirement, condition or practice is imposed that has, or is likely to have, the effect of disadvantaging people with a personal characteristic protected by law.

 

Workplace Violence, Bullying and Harassment includes any unwelcome conduct, meaning uninvited conduct or behaviour, and, or any behaviour that offends, humiliates, intimidates or undermines another person.

 

Workplace violence is any incident where an employee is physically attacked, harassed or threatened in the workplace.

 

 

 

Workplace Gender Equality Agency

The Equal Opportunity for Woman in the Workplace Act 1999 has been renamed to the Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012. The Act aims to promote and improve gender equality for both men and woman. Similarly, the government body Equal Opportunity for Women in the Workplace, has been renamed the Workplace Gender Equality Agency.

 

 

 

 

 


 

 

 

Policy 

 

Bagwan Health endorses diversity, supports equal rights. The organisation does not advocate, support or practice discrimination based on race, religion, age, national origin, language, sex, sexual orientation, or mental or physical handicap; whether covered by applicable legislation or not, except where affirmative action may be required to redress individual or social handicaps of people from disadvantaged groups.

 

 

Discrimination

Discrimination can occur when a person or group is treated less favourably than another person or group in a similar situation because of a personal characteristic protected by law.

 

Indirectly, discrimination can occur when an unreasonable requirement, condition or practice is imposed that has, or is likely to have, the effect of disadvantaging people with a personal characteristic protected by law.

 

Assumptions based on prejudice will have no place at Bagwan Health.

 

There shall be no discrimination on the grounds of:

●       age

●       disability, disease or injury, including a work-related injury

●       industrial activity/inactivity

●       sexual orientation, intersex status or general identity

●       marital status, including de facto relationships or same-sex relationship

●       physical features

●       political opinion

●       social origin

●       pregnancy and breastfeeding

●       race, colour, descent, national origin or ethnic background

●       religious belief or activity

●       sex

●       status as a parent or carer

●       medical record

●       personal association with someone of the above attributes.

 

It is also unlawful to request information, either verbally or in writing that may be used for discriminatory purposes and this requirement will be observed throughout Bagwan Health.

 

 

Workplace Violence, Bullying and Harassment

Everyone in the workplace must take reasonable care of their own health and safety, and for the health and safety of anyone else who may be affected by their acts or omissions in the workplace.

 

Bagwan Health will not tolerate any form of unlawful discrimination such as racial abuse, violence, or any form of bullying or harassment, in the workplace. This includes any unwelcome conduct, meaning uninvited conduct or behaviour, and, or any behaviour that offends, humiliates, intimidates or undermines another person.

 

Some other examples of inappropriate and unacceptable are:

●       verbal threats, and, or any form of threatening behaviour

●       unwelcome sexual comments

●       unwelcome physical contact

●       insulting someone because of their ethnic or racial origin

●       insults and or name-calling

●       spreading rumours

●       consistent talk about sex

●       crude jokes and conversation

●       sexual innuendo

●       following, phoning, sending emails and or other electronic messages

●       acting in any way that could reasonably be expected to arouse apprehension or fear.

 

 

Workplace Gender Equality Agency

The Equal Opportunity for Woman in the Workplace Act 1999 has been renamed to the Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012. The Act aims to promote and improve gender equality for both men and woman. Similarly, the government body Equal Opportunity for Women in the Workplace has been renamed the Workplace Gender Equality Agency.

 

 

Breastfeeding Friendly Workplace

Bagwan Health recognises the importance of breastfeeding for both mother and child, and as such, will endeavour to provide the support necessary to enable mothers to balance a continuation of breastfeeding with their return to work.

 

 

Equal Employment Opportunity for People with Disabilities

Bagwan Health is committed to providing an open and fair selection process for employment opportunities that are non-discriminatory and will enable people with disabilities to apply for vacant positions.

 


 

 

 

Procedures

 

Workplace Gender Equality (WGE)

In line with the WGE Act, Bagwan Health completes an annual report and ensures it is lodged by the required time.

 

Bagwan Health identifies several employment matters for consideration in the report.

 

They include, but are not limited to:

•           Recruitment and Selection

•           Promotion, Transfer and Termination of Employment

•           Work Organisation

•           Training and Development

•           Conditions of Service

•           Arrangements for dealing with Sex-Based Harassment

•           Arrangements for dealing with Pregnancy, Potential Pregnancy and Breastfeeding.

 

Other information Bagwan Health includes in the report consists of:

•           a profile of the workplace

•           possible future actions to take to implement the plan.

 

The completed report is published on the WGE website.


 

 

Complaints to Discrimination, Bullying and Harassment, Sexual Harassment, or Other Concerns

Any Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student who believes they may have been discriminated against, on any of the grounds listed, are encouraged to raise the matter with their Team Leader, Coordinator, Manager or another Manager.

 

The process for lodging a formal complaint is outlined in the Bagwan Health Complaints Handling Policy and Procedures. The complaint will be addressed with speed, sensitivity, confidentiality, professionalism and consistency.

 

Managers, Team Leaders and Coordinators must act fairly and impartially in relation to current and potential employees, volunteers and students. They must treat reports of possible discrimination seriously and sympathetically to investigate reports thoroughly.  They also must ensure that no one is disadvantaged or victimised as a result of a discrimination complaint being made or investigated. Managers must refer formal complaints to the Human Resources Manager and the CEO prior to action being taken.

 

Once all information has been gathered and all parties have been consulted, the relevant Manager will make a collective decision on whether, on the balance of probabilities, the complaint is sustained.

 

Irrespective of the findings of the investigation, the decision will be communicated to all relevant parties, together with an appropriate explanation.

 

 

 

 

 

Breaches to Equal Opportunity and Anti-discrimination Policy

If there is a breach of the Bagwan Health Equal Opportunity and Anti-discrimination Policy, disciplinary action will be taken, and serious breaches may result in dismissal.

 

Breast Feeding

The support Bagwan Health is able to provide to mothers may depend on the practicability of an employee being released from duties, for example, if an employee works one-on-one with a service user. Employees should first speak to their Manager to discuss how breastfeeding might be accommodated within their position.

 

Support may include the following.

 

▪        Lactation breaks to breastfeed or express milk can be organised in consultation with the employee’s supervisor. Breaks must be taken at a time that will not inconvenience or pose a danger to other staff and service users.

 

▪        Where possible, access to a private room with a comfortable chair to breastfeed and a refrigerator to store expressed milk. Employees should clearly label the milk as expressed milk.

 

▪        Access to information. Employees who are pregnant or considering pregnancy will be provided with this policy and are encouraged to discuss how to balance breastfeeding and work commitments with their supervisor.

 

▪        Flexible work options. A mother can negotiate flexible work options with her supervisor, such as job-sharing, permanent part-time and flexible starting and finishing times around core working hours.

 

All employees will be made aware of this policy. Co-workers must treat breastfeeding mothers with respect and dignity.

 

Equal Employment Opportunity for People with Disabilities

Selection decisions for Bagwan Health vacant positions are weighted between the written application, the applicant’s ability to meet the key selection criteria, the interview and the reference checks.

 

Bagwan Health is committed to facilitating appropriate support to enable people with disabilities to undertake employment and volunteering. This can include providing appropriate physical facilities, and access to technology and relevant health and safety planning and training.

 

Bagwan Health will keep annual data on the numbers of employees and volunteers who have required tailored employment support.

 

 

Roles and responsibilities

            Bagwan Health recognises its responsibilities for working within the following legislations:

·         Victorian Equal Opportunity Act 2010

·         Age Discrimination Act 2004

·         Disability Discrimination Act 1992

·         Sex Discrimination Act 1984

·         Racial Discrimination Act 1975

·         Australian Human Rights Commission Act 1986

·         Workplace Gender Equality Act 2012.

 

Bagwan Health believes that all employees are entitled to be treated on the basis of their true abilities and merit. and not affected by irrelevant personal characteristics. Employees are entitled to work in an environment which is free of discrimination, bullying and sexual harassment. Employees have the right to raise issues or make an enquiry or complaint in a reasonable and respectful manner without being victimised.

 

Bagwan Health employees are entitled to access employment, promotion, training, transfers and the benefits of employment on the basis of merit, and are assessed on the basis of their skills, qualifications, abilities, prior work performance and aptitudes.

 

All Bagwan Health human resource policies and procedures are based on the merit principle. This means selecting and/or rewarding the best person in each situation, and favouritism or quotas will not be tolerated.

 

The policy and related procedures will be reviewed on an annual basis or more frequently, if required, to ensure continued compliance with the relevant legislation.

 

 

 

 

The Board

 The Board will:

·                Regularly review the leadership and commitment given to eliminating discrimination, through active promotion of the organisation’s Anti-Discrimination Policy

·                Monitor performance by way of periodic management reports and assurances.

 

 

The CEO

The CEO will ensure the following.  

·                The organisation’s practices and processes incorporate precautions against discrimination in such areas as hiring, client selection, and program delivery.

·                Reasonable accommodations are made to allow diverse groups to access the benefits provided by the organization.

·                Where appropriate, weight is given to the culture and experiences of individuals from disadvantaged groups.

·                Where appropriate, delegate responsibility for compliance to officers with responsibility for particular sections.

·                Oversee the performance of subordinate officers in these matters.

·                Review and report to the Board, as appropriate, on the effectiveness of the management systems established to remove discrimination.

·                Analyse material breaches and identified compliance system weaknesses for systematic trends and ensure that any adverse trends are addressed.

·                Promote a culture of effective policy compliance across the organisation.

 

 

 

 

 

Managers and Supervisors

Managers and supervisors will:

·                Model appropriate standards of behaviour, take steps to educate and make staff aware of their obligations under this policy and the law

·                Intervene quickly and appropriately when they become aware of inappropriate behaviour, and act fairly to resolve issues

·                Enforce workplace standards, ensuring relevant parties are heard and refer formal complaints to the Human Resources Manager

·                Ensure new employees will be provided with a copy of the policy and procedure as part of their induction.

 

 

Employees

Employees, volunteers or students engaged in Bagwan Health will:

·                Ensure they are aware of the organisation’s policy against discrimination

·                Not act in a manner that would be discriminatory pursuant to this policy or any applicable legislation

·                Have a legal and moral responsibility to treat each other with dignity, courtesy and respect and are expected to fulfil these responsibilities as a condition of their employment.

Policy Name – Freedom of Information

Policy Number

Version Number

Scope

This policy applies to all staff and contractors employed by Bagwan Health, Allied Health professionals, Credentialed Specialists, students, patients and visitors.

Policy

The Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Vic) gives members of the public the right to access their records held by Bagwan Health. The Act also allows members of the public to request their records to be annotated or to request an explanation or summary of their records.

This policy defines the standards and processes associated with the request to access records under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Vic).

Procedure 

Most Freedom of Information (FOI) requests involve members of the public seeking access to documents containing their personal information. Individuals can also request access to documents containing other information, such as information about government policies, programs and decision-making processes.Categories of Documents

Categories of Documents

In the course of running Bagwan Health and carrying out our functions, a range of documents are created. The following is a non-exhaustive list of the types of documents that are either publicly available or available for access under the Freedom of Information Act 1982 (Vic):

·         Medical records

·         Contracts

·         Policies and procedures

·         Briefings and reports

·         Human resource records

·         Official correspondence

·         Meeting records

·         Financial records

·         Clinical training, research and education materials

 

·         Media releases.

Bagwan Health documents can be organised under the following categories:

·         Clinical operations – treatment records

·         Research and clinical training operations

·         Procurement and supply chain

·         Facilities and utilities

·         Business and strategic planning

·         Human resources

·         Finance

·         Legal

 

·         Policy.

Types of Patient Information

Medical and health information is collected during inpatient, outpatient or emergency attendances. The information is used to assist patients in their ongoing care and treatment. Such information includes details of current and past illnesses or injuries, operations, pathology results and medications taken/prescribed. 

Medical and health information is stored in many ways including paper, computer systems, film, tapes and x-rays.

Record keeping

Bagwan Health complies with the statutory requirements for information retention according to the Public Records Office of Victoria. The table below outlines the retention period for medical and health records.

Type of records

Retention period

Inpatient records

Generally 15 years after last attendance, or until the age of 25, whichever is the longest

Outpatient and emergency department records

Minimum of 12 years and up to 20 years from the last date of attendance

Psychiatric inpatient and outpatient records

Minimum of 25 years or until the age of 43, whichever is the longest

Radiology

Minimum of 5 years after creation

Records of deceased patients

12 years from the date of death

 

At the end of the retention period, records are disposed of in a secure manner.


Applications to Access Records

In accordance with the Freedom of Information Act (1992), all applications to access records must:

·         Be in writing (email and facsimile are acceptable)

·         Include sufficient detail to identify the correct documents covered by the request (e.g. full name of patient, date of birth; date of attendance or services accessed)

·         Give a mailing address in Australia where notices under the Act can be sent

·         Be lodged at Bagwan Health with any application fee payable under the regulations

 

·         Be accompanied by copies of two forms of ID e.g. drivers’ licence, Medicare card etc. 

Applications to access records must be made either in writing to the FOI Officer or by completing an Application Form from the Health Information Services department.

 

Applications to access records must be made either in writing to the FOI Officer or by completing an Application Form from the Health Information Services department.

 

 

Postal Applications:

 

Freedom of Information Officer

Health Information Services

PO Box 534

Bagwan Health, Victoria 3999

Email:

FOIrequest@bgh.gov.au

Non-personal Applications

Members of the public can obtain another person’s records if they can provide written authorisation from the person permitting access to their information.

If the application is for somebody that is deceased, then the applicant must provide identification that indicates that they are the closest relative to that person. If the applicant is not the closest relative, the applicant must provide written authorisation from the closest living relative permitting them access to the information.

A person may also obtain another person’s records if they can provide evidence that they:

·         Have Power of Attorney (medical)

 

·         Are a Legal Guardian of that person.

Can records be released outside FOI?

Records may be released to other healthcare providers for the continuing provision of health care (e.g. Emergency Department) and may also be released in accordance with due legal process (e.g. as evidence in a legal action before a court).

Cost

There are no fees or charges of the application if a member of the public requests their own personal information. An application fee of $30 is required for non-personal applications, and this must be paid when the application is lodged. Additional charges such as photocopying and staff time may be incurred, as per the Freedom of Information Act 1992.

Bagwan Health may waive or reduce the application fee in some instances, e.g. financial hardship, Health Care Card and Pension Card holders.

Cost

An application fee of $30 is required for non-personal applications, and this must be paid when the application is lodged. Additional charges such as photocopying and staff time may be incurred, as per the Freedom of Information Act 1992.

Bagwan Health may waive or reduce the application fee in some instances, e.g. financial hardship, Health Care Card and Pension Card holders.

Notice of Decision

Upon receipt of a valid application, Bagwan Health has a maximum of 45 calendar days to make a decision regarding access. At that time, the requester may also receive an invoice for any applicable charges. The charges must be paid in full before any documents are released. There may be circumstances where Bagwan Health will need to consult with the requester to extend the 30 day period.

When Access is Granted

When access is granted, copies of the documents will be available for collection from Bagwan Health. Alternatively, the documents can be sent to the requester via post.

Application to Amend Personal Information

Should the person requesting access believe that the personal information held by Bagwan Health is incorrect, incomplete, and out of date or misleading, they can then apply to have that information amended.

Application to amend personal information must be in writing, and the applicant must provide as much information as they can to show how or why the records need to be amended. The onus to provide this evidence falls with the applicant, not Bagwan Health.

Written reasons will be provided to the requester if their amendment is refused, as well as information about how they can apply for a review of the decision.

pages.title: Incident management
pages.html:
Policy Name

Incident Management

Policy Number

004

Owner of Policy 

Dr Christina Jones, CEO

Scope

This policy has been developed to ensure that all Bagwan Health employees understand the processes to be taken in the event of a dangerous occurrence or accident. This policy allows for a standardised system for managing clinical and corporate incidents to ensure health practitioners, managers and employees can respond effectively to them.

Bagwan Health recognises that the health and safety of its employees is a priority and that if accidents or incidents do occur, they should be reported. Incidents should be investigated to ensure that the possibility of recurrence or further risk is minimised.

Bagwan Health understands the importance of incident reporting and investigation and has developed hazard inspection, hazard reporting and maintenance programs to minimise the workplace accidents or dangerous occurrences.

The purpose of this policy is to provide direction to health services regarding the

management of clinical and corporate incidents. This includes appropriate feedback to patients, families/support persons and clinicians and the sharing of lessons learned to prevent patient harm.

This policy applies to all employees, volunteers, contractors and visitors under the control of Bagwan Health

 

Term and definitions 
Authorised person

An authorised person is the relevant Manager or the Chief Executive Officer.

 

Employee

An employee is a Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student on placement with Bagwan Health.

 

Individual

Individual refers to Bagwan Health service users, families and friends, employees, potential employees, volunteers, students and the community.

 

Service user

A service user is a child or an adult (person with a disability) or aged person who uses a Bagwan Health service.

 

Workplace

A workplace includes working on-site or off-site, attendance at a work-related conference or function, and attendance at a client or other work-related event, including retreats and social events.

 

Incident

Incident refers to any event which causes or could have caused injury, illness, damage to plant, equipment, vehicles, property, material, or the environment or public alarm. It also includes losses of containment, fire, explosion, non-compliance with environmental regulatory requirements, vehicle incidents and off-site incidents.

 

Hazard

Hazard refers to a source or situation with a potential for harm in terms of human injury or ill health, damage to property, damage to the environment or a combination of these.

 

DHHS

DHHS refers to the Department of Health and Human Services.

 

CIMS

CIMS refers to Client Incident Management System.

 

DINMA

DINMA refers to Disease/Injury/Near Miss/Accident Report.

 

NDIS or DHIS funded services

NDIS or DHHS funded services: the DHHS CIMS (Client Incident Management System) online web-based tool (for Major and Non-Major Impact on service users only) or Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting tool (for Cat 1, 2 and 3 not impacting on service users and Cat 3 impacting on service users). These are online web-based questionnaires that are required to be completed promptly by an employee, volunteer or student to report that an incident has occurred.

 

DET funded services

DET funded services: for Department of Education and Training (DET) funded services we will follow DHHS reporting guidelines, i.e. CIMS or Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting (Cat 1, 2 and 3 not impacting on service users), see above.

 

Department of Health (Commonwealth) / CHSP funded services

Department of Health (Commonwealth) / CHSP funded services: for DH funded services, i.e. CHSP (Commonwealth Home Support Programme), the Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting Tool need to be filled out for incidents impacting on service users and staff, volunteers and students. Bagwan Health will keep a record of any incidents or risks involving service delivery to service users and will only report serious incidents (category one/major) to DSS (carer.support.vic@dss.gov).

All incident reports must include a complete, sequential, factual and account of the events. 

Incidents impacting on service users (CIMS Incident Reporting Tool).

 

Major impact and Non-major impact

‘Major impact’ and ‘non-major impact’ are used to define the two DHHS incident categories. In determining the category of the incident, the focus must be on the impact (level of harm) to the service user. While the most senior staff member present is responsible for completing the initial incident report, the management of the service provider is responsible for using their professional judgement to confirm the assessment of the appropriate categorisation for the incident, based on the guidance set out in this section.

The following three sections set out the definitions of these categories (2 DHHS + 1 Bagwan Health).

 

Major impact

Major impact on the service user include:

• The unanticipated death of a service user

• Severe physical, emotional or psychological injury or suffering which is likely to cause ongoing trauma

• A pattern of incidents related to one service user which, when taken together, meet the level of harm to a service user-defined above. This may be the case even if each individual incident is a non-major impact incident.

In addition, certain incidents such as all deaths of service users in unexpected or unanticipated circumstances, including suicides, must be reported as major impact incidents.

 

Non-major impact

Non-major impact on the service user include:

• Incidents that cause physical, emotional or psychological injury or suffering, without resulting in major impact as defined above

• Impacts to the service user which do not require significant changes to care requirements, other than short-term interventions (for example, first aid, observation, talking interventions or short-term medical treatment)

• Incidents that involve a service user but result in minimal harm

• Incidents that do not otherwise meet the criteria for ‘major impact’ above.

 

Minor impact

Minor impact on the service user:

Incidents NOT impacting on service users (Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting).

There is now one Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting Tool, where staff can fill out incident reports for all incidents where service users are NOT impacted and for minor (Cat 3) to service users.

If medical attention is required for staff, Bagwan Health encourages staff to complete a DINMA (Disease/Injury/Near Miss/Accident) Report.

 

Policy 

Bagwan Health commits to preventing workplace accidents and minimising dangerous occurrences and will endeavour to achieve a zero accident rate.

Bagwan Health will:

• Provide a mechanism for reporting accidents, incidents, work-related illness and dangerous occurrences

• Investigate accidents to determine the root cause with the objective of preventing a recurrence

• Obtain statistical information about the accident or incidents

• Meet legislative requirements for reporting accidents and incidents.

All accidents or incidents that result in an injury or work-related illness during the course of work must immediately be reported to the Regional Occupational Health and Safety Representative and First Aid Officer.

Any dangerous occurrence which has the potential to result in injury or damage to property must be reported in the same manner as an accident.

In the event of a dangerous occurrence or accident, Bagwan Health must ensure the relevant state authority is notified and that a full investigation is undertaken to determine the root cause.

The most appropriate corrective action will be taken to ensure the incident does not recur.

 

Bagwan Health manages incidents based on the following principles: 

Obligation to act

Key stakeholders acknowledge and understand their roles and responsibilities in the incident management.

 

Just culture

Incidents are reported and acknowledged without fear of blame or retribution and individuals are treated fairly in an open and honest manner.

 

Openness about failures

Incidents are reported and acknowledged without fear of inappropriate blame. Patients and their families/support persons are offered an apology and told what went wrong and why.

 

Emphasis about learning

The system is oriented towards learning from mistakes and consistently employs improvement methods for achieving this Obligation to act – the obligation to take action to remedy problems is clearly accepted and the allocation of this responsibility is unambiguous and explicit.

 

Accountability

The limits of individual accountability are clear, individuals understand when they may be held accountable for their actions.

 

Appropriate prioritisation about action

Action to address problems is prioritised and resources directed to the areas where the greatest improvements are possible.

 

Cooperation, collaboration and communication

Teamwork is recognised as the best defence of system failures and is explicitly encouraged and fostered within a culture of trust and mutual respect. Bagwan Health commits to preventing workplace accidents and minimising dangerous occurrences and will endeavour to achieve a zero accident rate.

 

Procedure

When an incident occurs at Bagwan Health, a series of actions must follow. The importance of identifying these as separate steps is to ensure that all appropriate action is taken. 

 

Timeline for reporting incidents

• CIMS Major must be reported to DHHs within 24 hrs and logged by employees.

• CIMS Non-Major must be reported to DHHs within 30 days and logged by employees within 2 working days (or on Monday if the incident happened over the weekend).

• Bagwan Health ‘serious’ (Category 1) internal incidents must be reported within one working day (or Monday if the incident happened over the weekend).

• Bagwan Health less serious (Category 2 and 3) Internal incidents must be reported by staff within 1 working days (or on Monday if the incident happened over the weekend) in line with the WGE Act.

 

The 5 Stages of Incident Management

There are 5 stages to effective incident management:

• Stage 1 – Identification and response

• Stage 2 – Reporting

• Stage 3 – Incident investigation

• Stage 4 – Incident review

• Stage 5 – Analysis and learning.

 

Stage 1: Identification and response 

• Identification is when an incident is disclosed to, or observed by, a service provider at any service delivery setting (for example, provider premises, outreach location or a service user’s home). This may include disclosure by a service user, family member or other professionals, to the service provider.

• Response covers the immediate activities undertaken to ensure the safety and wellbeing of service users, staff and visitors, preserve evidence and notify emergency services and family or other support people.

 

Stage 2: Reporting

• Reporting captures specific information about the incident. As part of this stage, follow up is undertaken to ensure the information provided in an incident notification is accurate, and Bagwan Health and the department are assured that appropriate actions are being planned and/or undertaken to manage the incident.

 

Stage 3: Incident investigation

• An investigation is a formal process of collecting information to ascertain the facts about an incident, which may inform any subsequent criminal, civil, disciplinary or administrative sanctions.

• In the context of this policy, the purpose of an incident investigation is to determine whether there has been abuse or poor quality of care of a service user by a staff member, carer or another service user.

• Incident investigations may be carried out by Bagwan Health or external bodies (including the department).

 

Stage 4: Incident review

• A review is an analysis of an incident to identify what happened, determine whether an incident was managed appropriately, identify likely causes of the incident, and to apply subsequent learnings to reduce the risk of future harm.

• Incident reviews may be carried out by Bagwan Health or external bodies (including the department).

 

Stage 5: Analysis and learning

• Analysis and learning includes monitoring and acting on trends identified through the analysis of incident information, to enhance the quality of service and supports service users.

• Reporting, investigating, reviewing and analysing incidents helps Bagwan Health to review and assess the way in which an incident has been managed, to implement improvements, minimise risk and embed a continuous improvement approach. This supports better service user experience and outcomes.

 

Child abuse and neglect incidents 

The Victorian Reportable Conduct Scheme is operational from 1 July 2017. The scheme will require the centralised reporting of allegations of child abuse against workers or volunteers in relevant organisations with a high level of responsibility for children. 

The scheme will be introduced in three phases from July 2017:

• Phase 1: From 1 July 2017, the scheme will apply to child protection, out-of-home care services, residential services for children with a disability, certain education providers, government and non-government schools and government departments (including youth justice services).

• Phase 2: From 1 January 2018 the scheme will apply to hospitals, other disability services for children, providers of overnight camps, religious bodies and the residential facilities of boarding schools.

• Phase 3: From 1 January 2019, the scheme will apply to early childhood services and certain statutory bodies that have responsibility for children, such as public museums and galleries.

 

The reportable conduct scheme will require allegations of suspected criminal conduct to be reported to Victoria Police as the first priority and will maintain the primacy of an investigation by Victoria Police of any allegations of criminal misconduct. In all circumstances, allegations of criminal conduct must be reported to Victoria Police as the first priority.

For child abuse and neglect incidents, the On-Call Management or Division Manager and CEO need to be informed immediately. Bagwan Health CEO (or her delegate) must report any allegation of reportable conduct to the Commission for Children and Young People within three business days of becoming aware of the allegation. It is a criminal offence for the Bagwan Health CEO to fail to notify (within three business days) and update (within 30 calendar days) the Commission for Children and Young People (CCYP) about reportable allegations.

Note: the reporting to the Commission for Children and Young People by Bagwan Health CEO complements/is in addition to all the current steps we are required to undertake when an allegation of child abuse (sexual, physical and psychological) or significant neglect is made.

See for details as well Child Safe policy (2702) and Responding to Alleged Physical or Sexual Assault (2608).

 

Incident Severity Rating (ISR)

The ISR methodology provides a more consistent classification of incident severity. It also allows incident data to be mapped to a variety of other methodologies.

The ISR methodology can be consistently applied across all clinical (patient) and occupational health and safety (OHS) incidents.

The ISR is based on:

• the actual and potential impact on those involved in the incident

• the actual and potential impact on the organisation.

The impact on the people involved is automatically derived from three related questions, these are:

• degree of impact

• level of care

• treatment required.

 

Bagwan Health will derive an ISR depending on the values selected by the end-user in each of the three lead questions.

 

[enter table here – page 12] 

 

 

Definition – degree of impact

Where harm includes disease, injury, suffering, disability and death:

• Disease – a physiological or psychological dysfunction

• Injury – damage to tissues caused by an agent or circumstance

• Suffering – experiencing anything subjectively unpleasant. This may include pain, malaise nausea, vomiting, loss (any negative consequence, including financial) depression, agitation, alarm, fear or grief

• Disability – any type of impairment of body structure or function, activity limitation restriction of participation in society, associated with a past or present harm.

 

[enter table here – page 13] 

 

 

Definition – level of care

 

[enter table here – page 14] 

 

 

Definition – treatment required

 

[enter table here – page 15] 

Roles and responsibilities

An incident report – Online Tool or Bagwan Health’s Internal Incident Reporting Tool/s – must be completed by the employee who witnessed the incident. If there were no witnesses, it must be completed by the employee to whom the incident was reported.

The policy and related procedures will be reviewed on an annual basis or more frequently, if required, to ensure continued compliance with the relevant legislation.

 

The CEO

The CEO will ensure that: 

• The organisation has systems in place to report, investigate and monitor actions necessary to reduce the likelihood of incidents recurring

• Sufficient mechanisms are in place to enable the effective reporting, recording, investigation and implementation of recommendations as a result of an incident

• That staff are encouraged (and supported) to report incidents and near-miss events as a proactive preventative measure

• Those recommendations derived from incident investigations are appropriately addressed and their effectiveness is evaluated

• Analysis of incident data is made available to the organisation’s clinical governance committee (or equivalent) for review 

• The principles of open disclosure are observed when interacting with patients and their families or carers when an incident occurs, and that these principles guide the overall management of the incident

• That all sentinel events and clinical incidents where the organisation has identified system or process issues directly contributed to the incident outcome; are reported to the department accordingly

• The Manager (Division) or CEO to report to DHHS Major incidents within 24 hrs to DHHS.

 

Managers and Supervisors

Managers and supervisors will ensure that:

• An online incident report  has been completed and reporting processes have been followed within required timelines and all other required reports are completed

• The service user’s family are informed of incidents that involve injury or hospitalisation of their relative, according to agreed arrangements and of all allegations of physical and/or sexual assault

• Ensure service users are offered medical assistance and counselling

• Communication strategies have been followed to ensure all relevant employee, volunteer or students are aware of the incident and any recommendations or control measures that may prevent or reduce the risk of the incident reoccurring

• Analysis of incident trends and Implementation of recommendations and or control measures is documented

• Community Visitors are informed of any service user death

• Reporting to the Board any Major and Non-Major incidents and incidents reported on the Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting Tool at the next scheduled meeting, or immediately if there are serious immediate implications for the organisation

• The Manager (Division) or CEO to report to DHHS Major incidents within 24 hrs to DHHS

• Investigate and assess each incident and develop control measures and risk management plans accordingly. This can be done by using the online CIMS tools in case of an incident impacting on service users (DHHS and NDIS funded services)

• Analyse the events in order to add any relevant information to Occupational Violence Risk Assessments or Client Behaviour Support Plans

• Ensure Incident Report findings and recommendations are recorded for Continuous Improvement towards Risk Management, OH&S and Quality systems.

 

Employees

Employees, volunteers or students engaged in Bagwan Health will ensure that:

• Whenever an incident occurs staff need to complete the relevant electronic/online incident report  

• For serious incidents, the Employee, volunteer or students must inform the team leader, program manager or On-Call Management immediately and fill-out the online tool as soon as possible as Bagwan Health needs to report to DHHS within 24 hrs. For Non-Major Incidents, the timeline is two days

• Inform the service user’s family of incidents that involve injury or hospitalisation of their relative, according to agreed arrangements and of all allegations of physical and/or sexual assault

• Complete any other reports required such as the online DINMA report, service user case notes etc. 

• Employees who are unsure of the category of an incident should treat the report as being at a higher level.

Just culture Incidents are reported and acknowledged without fear of blame or retribution and individuals are treated fairly in an open and honest manner. Openness about failures Incidents are reported and acknowledged without fear of inappropriate blame. Patients and their families/support persons are offered an apology and told what went wrong and why. Emphasis about learning The system is oriented towards learning from mistakes and consistently employs improvement methods for achieving this Obligation to act – the obligation to take action to remedy problems is clearly accepted and the allocation of this responsibility is unambiguous and explicit. Accountability The limits of individual accountability are clear, individuals understand when they may be held accountable for their actions. Appropriate prioritisation about action Action to address problems is prioritised and resources directed to the areas where the greatest improvements are possible. Cooperation, collaboration and communication Teamwork is recognised as the best defence of system failures and is explicitly encouraged and fostered within a culture of trust and mutual respect. Bagwan Health commits to preventing workplace accidents and minimising dangerous occurrences and will endeavour to achieve a zero accident rate. Procedure When an incident occurs at Bagwan Health, a series of actions must follow. The importance of identifying these as separate steps is to ensure that all appropriate action is taken. Timeline for reporting incidents • C IMS Major must be reported to DHHs within 24 hrs and logged by employees. • C IMS Non-Major must be reported to DHHs within 30 days and logged by employees within 2 working days (or on Monday if the incident happened over the weekend). • Bagwan Health ‘serious’ (Category 1) internal incidents must be reported within one working day (or Monday if the incident happened over the weekend). • Bagwan Health less serious (Category 2 and 3) Internal incidents must be reported by staff within 1 working days (or on Monday if the incident happened over the weekend) in line with the WGE Act. The 5 Stages of Incident Management There are 5 stages to effective incident management: • Stage 1 – Identification and response • Stage 2 – Reporting • Stage 3 – Incident investigation • Stage 4 – Incident review • Stage 5 – Analysis and learning. Stage 1: Identification and response • Identification is when an incident is disclosed to, or observed by, a service provider at any service delivery setting (for example, provider premises, outreach location or a service user’s home). This may include disclosure by a service user, family member or other professionals, to the service provider. • Response covers the immediate activities undertaken to ensure the safety and wellbeing of service users, staff and visitors, preserve evidence and notify emergency services and family or other support people. Stage 2: Reporting • Reporting captures specific information about the incident. As part of this stage, follow up is undertaken to ensure the information provided in an incident notification is accurate, and Bagwan Health and the department are assured that appropriate actions are being planned and/or undertaken to manage the incident. Stage 3: Incident investigation • An investigation is a formal process of collecting information to ascertain the facts about an incident, which may inform any subsequent criminal, civil, disciplinary or administrative sanctions. • In the context of this policy, the purpose of an incident investigation is to determine whether there has been abuse or poor quality of care of a service user by a staff member, carer or another service user. • Incident investigations may be carried out by Bagwan Health or external bodies (including the department). Stage 4: Incident review • A review is an analysis of an incident to identify what happened, determine whether an incident was managed appropriately, identify likely causes of the incident, and to apply subsequent learnings to reduce the risk of future harm. • Incident reviews may be carried out by Bagwan Health or external bodies (including the department). Stage 5: Analysis and learning • Analysis and learning includes monitoring and acting on trends identified through the analysis of incident information, to enhance the quality of service and supports service users. • Reporting, investigating, reviewing and analysing incidents helps Bagwan Health to review and assess the way in which an incident has been managed, to implement improvements, minimise risk and embed a continuous improvement approach. This supports better service user experience and outcomes. Child abuse and neglect incidents The Victorian Reportable Conduct Scheme is operational from 1 July 2017. The scheme will require the centralised reporting of allegations of child abuse against workers or volunteers in relevant organisations with a high level of responsibility for children. The scheme will be introduced in three phases from July 2017: • Phase 1: From 1 July 2017, the scheme will apply to child protection, out-of-home care services, residential services for children with a disability, certain education providers, government and non-government schools and government departments (including youth justice services). • Phase 2: From 1 January 2018 the scheme will apply to hospitals, other disability services for children, providers of overnight camps, religious bodies and the residential facilities of boarding schools. • Phase 3: From 1 January 2019, the scheme will apply to early childhood services and certain statutory bodies that have responsibility for children, such as public museums and galleries. The reportable conduct scheme will require allegations of suspected criminal conduct to be reported to Victoria Police as the first priority and will maintain the primacy of an investigation by Victoria Police of any allegations of criminal misconduct. In all circumstances, allegations of criminal conduct must be reported to Victoria Police as the first priority. For child abuse and neglect incidents, the On-Call Management or Division Manager and CEO need to be informed immediately. Bagwan Health CEO (or her delegate) must report any allegation of reportable conduct to the Commission for Children and Young People within three business days of becoming aware of the allegation. It is a criminal offence for the Bagwan Health CEO to fail to notify (within three business days) and update (within 30 calendar days) the Commission for Children and Young People (CCYP) about reportable allegations. Note: the reporting to the Commission for Children and Young People by Bagwan Health CEO complements/is in addition to all the current steps we are required to undertake when an allegation of child abuse (sexual, physical and psychological) or significant neglect is made. See for details as well Child Safe policy (2702) and Responding to Alleged Physical or Sexual Assault (2608). Incident Severity Rating (ISR) The ISR methodology provides a more consistent classification of incident severity. It also allows incident data to be mapped to a variety of other methodologies. The ISR methodology can be consistently applied across all clinical (patient) and occupational health and safety (OHS) incidents. The ISR is based on: • the actual and potential impact on those involved in the incident • the actual and potential impact on the organisation. The impact on the people involved is automatically derived from three related questions, these are: • degree of impact • level of care • treatment required. Bagwan Health will derive an ISR depending on the values selected by the end-user in each of the three lead questions. [enter table here – page 12] Definition – degree of impact Where harm includes disease, injury, suffering, disability and death: • Disease – a physiological or psychological dysfunction • Injury – damage to tissues caused by an agent or circumstance • Suffering – experiencing anything subjectively unpleasant. This may include pain, malaise nausea, vomiting, loss (any negative consequence, including financial) depression, agitation, alarm, fear or grief • Disability – any type of impairment of body structure or function, activity limitation restriction of participation in society, associated with a past or present harm. [enter table here – page 13] Definition – level of care [enter table here – page 14] Definition – treatment required [enter table here – page 15] Roles and responsibilities An incident report – Online Tool or Bagwan Health’s Internal Incident Reporting Tool/s – must be completed by the employee who witnessed the incident. If there were no witnesses, it must be completed by the employee to whom the incident was reported. The policy and related procedures will be reviewed on an annual basis or more frequently, if required, to ensure continued compliance with the relevant legislation. The CEO The CEO will ensure that: • The organisation has systems in place to report, investigate and monitor actions necessary to reduce the likelihood of incidents recurring • Sufficient mechanisms are in place to enable the effective reporting, recording, investigation and implementation of recommendations as a result of an incident • That staff are encouraged (and supported) to report incidents and near-miss events as a proactive preventative measure • Those recommendations derived from incident investigations are appropriately addressed and their effectiveness is evaluated • Analysis of incident data is made available to the organisation’s clinical governance committee (or equivalent) for review • The principles of open disclosure are observed when interacting with patients and their families or carers when an incident occurs, and that these principles guide the overall management of the incident • That all sentinel events and clinical incidents where the organisation has identified system or process issues directly contributed to the incident outcome; are reported to the department accordingly • The Manager (Division) or CEO to report to DHHS Major incidents within 24 hrs to DHHS. Managers and Supervisors Managers and supervisors will ensure that: • An online incident report  has been completed and reporting processes have been followed within required timelines and all other required reports are completed • The service user’s family are informed of incidents that involve injury or hospitalisation of their relative, according to agreed arrangements and of all allegations of physical and/or sexual assault • Ensure service users are offered medical assistance and counselling • Communication strategies have been followed to ensure all relevant employee, volunteer or students are aware of the incident and any recommendations or control measures that may prevent or reduce the risk of the incident reoccurring • Analysis of incident trends and Implementation of recommendations and or control measures is documented • Community Visitors are informed of any service user death • Reporting to the Board any Major and Non-Major incidents and incidents reported on the Bagwan Health Internal Incident Reporting Tool at the next scheduled meeting, or immediately if there are serious immediate implications for the organisation • The Manager (Division) or CEO to report to DHHS Major incidents within 24 hrs to DHHS • Investigate and assess each incident and develop control measures and risk management plans accordingly. This can be done by using the online CIMS tools in case of an incident impacting on service users (DHHS and NDIS funded services) • Analyse the events in order to add any relevant information to Occupational Violence Risk Assessments or Client Behaviour Support Plans • Ensure Incident Report findings and recommendations are recorded for Continuous Improvement towards Risk Management, OH&S and Quality systems. Employees Employees, volunteers or students engaged in Bagwan Health will ensure that: • Whenever an incident occurs staff need to complete the relevant electronic/online incident report • For serious incidents, the Employee, volunteer or students must inform the team leader, program manager or On-Call Management immediately and fill-out the online tool as soon as possible as Bagwan Health needs to report to DHHS within 24 hrs. For Non-Major Incidents, the timeline is two days • Inform the service user’s family of incidents that involve injury or hospitalisation of their relative, according to agreed arrangements and of all allegations of physical and/or sexual assault • Complete any other reports required such as the online DINMA report, service user case notes etc. • Employees who are unsure of the category of an incident should treat the report as being at a higher level. pages.title: Infection control
pages.html:
Policy Name – Infection control

Scope

This policy applies to all staff and contractors employed by Bagwan Health, Allied Health professionals, Credentialed Specialists, students, patients and visitors.

Policy 

Under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 2004, Bagwan Health is obligated to provide a safe workplace for their staff, including the provision of adequate infection control procedures and the right equipment and training.

Using personal protective equipment (PPE) and adhering to infection control procedures will reduce the transmission of pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, protozoa or fungi and provide protection for health care workers.

This policy defines the standards and processes associated with the use of personal protective equipment within the context of infection control only. Requirements for personal protective equipment outside of those used for infection control are not included in this procedure.

Procedure

 

Assumption of Risk

The basis of good infection control is to assume that everyone is potentially infectious and that proper procedures have to be followed at all times.

 

Personal Protection Equipment (PPE)

PPE is to be put on immediately prior to entering the room of an infectious patient and removed upon leaving the room. It is not to be worn throughout the ward, as this increases the risk of transmitting infection to patients.

PPE will be supplied and available in each clinical area or department at Bagwan Health. Staff shall wear the appropriate PPE whenever it is likely that they will come into contact with blood or body fluids from any patient. Personal protective equipment can include gowns, aprons, masks, gloves, protective eyewear and face shields.

Visitors are required to adhere to infection control policies by way of performing basic hand hygiene before and after visiting. If visiting patients in isolation, visitors are required to adhere to the specific instructions for the type of isolation, which includes gloves, aprons/gowns and masks when required. All visitors are encouraged to not visit other patients after they have visited an infectious patient.

Staff will be trained in the donning and removal of PPE in orientation.

 

Gowns

Gowns and aprons are worn to protect skin and/or clothing from becoming contaminated, soiled or wet from contact with blood or body substances.

Plastic aprons form part of the Routine Contact Precautions. Plastic gowns are long-sleeved and are required in instances where Intensive Contact Precautions are required.

The types of protective clothing used at Bagwan Health include:

·         Disposable plastic aprons which are suitable for most situations

·         Long-sleeved, disposable fluid-resistant gowns which are used when there is an elevated risk of contamination or for contact isolation.

Masks

Masks are worn when there is potential for the mucous membranes in the mouth and nose to be exposed to blood or body substances. Masks prevent the spread of micro-organisms from staff to patients and protect staff from inhaling infectious aerosols or droplets, smoke or plume or other airborne hazards.

The types of masks used at Bagwan Health include:

·         Surgical Masks which are used in wards, departments and operating theatres

·         N95 Particulate Masks which are used when caring for patients with suspected or diagnosed airborne infectious diseases.

 

Gloves

Gloves are worn when there is potential for the hands to be exposed to blood or body substances. When gloves are worn and used appropriately they reduce the likelihood of hand contamination and minimise the risk that a health care worker will become infected. Gloves also reduce the likelihood that staff will transmit micro-organisms from their hands to patients.

Single-use gloves in a range of sizes are available and accessible in all areas.

The types of gloves used at Bagwan Health:

·         Non-sterile gloves which are suitable for most situations

·         Sterile gloves which are worn for surgical procedures where asepsis must be maintained.

It is recommended that staff involved in surgical procedures double-glove for extra protection.

 

Protection Eyewear and Face Protection

Protective eyewear and face protection are worn when there is potential for the mucous membranes in the mouth, nose or eyes to be exposed to blood or body substances.

The types of eyewear and face protection used at Bagwan Health include:

·         Goggles

·         Safety glasses with side shields

·         Mask with attached visor

·         Chin length plastic face shield.

 

Safety Precautions

Appropriate safety precautions should be taken when donning and removing PPE. This includes hand hygiene and the proper handling of items in the patient environment.

 

Donning PPE

First, perform hand hygiene and then prior to entering the patient’s room, put on PPE in the following order:

1.    Gown

·         Fully cover torso from neck to knees, arms to wrists, and wrap around the back

·         Fasten in back at neck and waist.

2.    Mask

·         Ensure the coloured side is outward

·         Secure ties above and below ears or place the elastic loops around ears

·         Flatten flexible metal band over the nose

·         Fit snug to face and below the chin.

3.    Protective eyewear and face protection

·         Put over face and/or eyes and adjust to fit

4.    Gloves

·         Extend to cover wrist of gown.

 

Removing PPE

Remove PPE before leaving the patient’s room in the following order:

1.    Gloves

·         Grasp the outside of the glove with the opposite gloved hand and peel off

·         Hold the removed glove in the gloved hand

·         Slide fingers of un-gloved hand under remaining glove at the wrist

·         Discard into a yellow waste bag

·         Perform hand hygiene.

2.    Protective eyewear and face protection

·         To remove, handle by ‘clean’ headband or earpieces

·         Place in the designated receptacle for reprocessing

·         Perform hand hygiene.

3.    Gown

·         Unfasten neck, then waist ties

·         Using a peeling motion; pull gown from each shoulder toward the same hand

·         The gown will turn inside out

·         Hold gown away from body, roll into a bundle and discard into a yellow waste bag

·         Perform hand hygiene.

4. Mask

·         Grasp from bottom to the top of ties/elastics and remove

·         Place in waste receptacle

·         Perform hand hygiene

 

Handling Contaminated Sharps 

When handling needles and other sharp contaminated objects:

·         Handle by the barrel

·         Never attempt to re-cap or bend used needles

·         Place in an appropriate puncture-proof container – a yellow container, labelled ‘Danger contaminated sharps’ and marked with a black biohazard symbol.

 

Outbreak Management

Bagwan Health is required to implement an outbreak management plan when risk assessment identifies the presence of a serious disease that has the potential to spread within the hospital environment or community.

 

Identification of a Potential Outbreak

An outbreak may be identified by:

·         Staff

·         Monitoring systems

·         Laboratory data 

·         Regional Public Health, national or international alerts.

The Infection Prevention & Control Nurse and the Director of Clinical Services will be notified to instigate a risk assessment.

 

Risk Assessment

A risk assessment will be conducted to evaluate the certainty of the infection. This will be conducted by a Microbiologist or appropriate physician. 

The risks assessment will be based on the following guidelines:

·         Contagiousness of the disease

·         Severity of the disease

·         Number of people affected

·         Legal requirements for notification to the Medical Officer of Health

 

 

Key issues to be considered:

·         People with the infection are being appropriately cared for

·         Staff providing care are protecting their own health

·         Potentially exposed persons are correctly identified and informed

·         Risk of infection to others is reduced by implementing control measures.

 

Communicate and inform

The following staff must be informed:

·         Infection Prevention & Control Committee

·         Credentialed Specialists

·         Senior Nursing Team and Executive

·         Medical Officer of Health as required

·         Ministry of Health as required.

 

Formation of an Outbreak Committee

If an outbreak occurs, then an Outbreak Committee is formed to:

·         Gather information

·         Plan strategy

·         Implement control measures

·         Communicate with patients, staff, credentialed specialists, other appropriate external agencies. They may also assist the CEO with media management.

 

Evaluation

·         Debrief

·         Evaluation of the efficacy of outbreak prevention and control measures will be completed by the Infection Prevention and Control Nurse

·         Infection Prevention and Control nurse will provide a written report to the Infection Prevention and Control Committee.

 

Control Measures

Will be determined by the Outbreak Committee.

 


Appendix One: Types of Precautions for Infection Control 

Standard Precautions: For all patients at all times.

 

Component

Actions required

Hand hygiene

Hand hygiene is carried out effectively according to the ‘5 moments for hand hygiene’.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)

Proper use of PPE which includes:

  • Gloves worn by staff when there is contact with bodily fluids, blood, soiled equipment or linen or performing invasive procedures requiring asepsis
  • Plastic aprons or gowns are used to minimise the risk of staff exposure to bodily fluids
  • Masks, eye shields or safety goggles are worn when staff are at risk of a splash of bodily fluids or blood.

Management of sharps

Sharps are disposed of in the dedicated sharps bins located in each room. To minimise the risk of needlestick injuries staff must:

  • Use safety devices where appropriate and available
  • Never recap a used needle
  • Use a dedicated dish to transport the needle and avoid placing fingers into the dish with the used needle. The dish should be for the sharps alone, and not be used to carry other items
  • Dispose of the used needle immediately after use.        

Linen

Used linen should be handled as though it is contaminated with bodily fluids. This means that:

  • Appropriate PPE is worn when handling used linen
  • Linen skips are taken to the patient bedside and are used to dispose of the used linen before placing the linen skip back in its designated location
  • Each isolation room will have its own linen skip.

Patients

Patients are informed of the importance of hand hygiene.

Visitors

Visitors are to perform hand hygiene when entering and leaving the patient care areas.

 

 

 

Routine Contact Precautions: For patients isolated with VRE vanB, MRSA, ESBL and shingles limited to one dermatome.

Component

Action required

PPE
(staff and visitors)

Plastic apron and hand hygiene.

Patient location

Allocation of a single room is preferred with own bathroom. Patients with VRE vanB can be cohorted providing that they have not been on antibiotics for the past 6 months and are continent of faeces.

Patient equipment

Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If the equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room.

 

 

Enhanced contact precautions: For patients isolated with gastroenteritis (or suspected) and clostridium difficile.

Component

Action required

PPE
(staff and visitors)

Hand hygiene

Plastic apron

Gloves

Surgical mask if patient vomiting.

Patient location

Allocation of a single room with own bathroom.

Patient equipment

Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If the equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room.

 

 

Intensive contact precautions: For patients isolated with VRE vanA, CPE, scabies or multi-resistant gram-negative organisms.

Component

Action required

PPE
(staff and visitors)

Hand hygiene

Long-sleeved plastic gown

Gloves (non-sterile)

Patient location

Allocation of a single room with own bathroom.

Patient equipment

Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If the equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room.


Droplet precautions: For patients isolated with influenza, rubella or meningococcal disease.

Component

Action required

PPE
(staff and visitors)

Hand hygiene

Plastic apron

Surgical mask

Patient location

Allocation of a single room with own bathroom. Door to the room to remain closed.

 If a patient is located in a shared room, place a surgical mask on the patient, close the privacy curtains around the patient and ensure at least 1 metre between patients. Patient must be moved into a single room as soon as possible.

Patient equipment

Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room.


Airborne precautions: For patients isolated with pulmonary tuberculosis, chickenpox or measles.

Component

Action required

PPE
(staff and visitors)

Hand hygiene

N95 mask

Patient location

Allocation of a negative pressure isolation room with anteroom. Both sets of doors are to be kept closed to maintain the negative pressure.

Patient equipment

Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room.

Upon patient discharge

The room should remain in negative pressure for a minimum of 30 minutes of the patient leaving. If any staff are entering the room within this 30 minute period, they are to still wear the N95 mask.

This means that: Appropriate PPE is worn when handling used linen Linen skips are taken to the patient bedside and are used to dispose of the used linen before placing the linen skip back in its designated location Each isolation room will have its own linen skip. Patients Patients are informed of the importance of hand hygiene. Visitors Visitors are to perform hand hygiene when entering and leaving the patient care areas. Routine Contact Precautions: For patients isolated with VRE vanB, MRSA, ESBL and shingles limited to one dermatome. Component Action required PPE (staff and visitors) Plastic apron and hand hygiene. Patient location Allocation of a single room is preferred with own bathroom. Patients with VRE vanB can be cohorted providing that they have not been on antibiotics for the past 6 months and are continent of faeces. Patient equipment Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If the equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room. Enhanced contact precautions: For patients isolated with gastroenteritis (or suspected) and clostridium difficile. Component Action required PPE (staff and visitors) Hand hygiene Plastic apron Gloves Surgical mask if patient vomiting. Patient location Allocation of a single room with own bathroom. Patient equipment Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If the equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room. Intensive contact precautions: For patients isolated with VRE vanA, CPE, scabies or multi-resistant gram-negative organisms. Component Action required PPE (staff and visitors) Hand hygiene Long-sleeved plastic gown Gloves (non-sterile) Patient location Allocation of a single room with own bathroom. Patient equipment Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If the equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room. Droplet precautions: For patients isolated with influenza, rubella or meningococcal disease. Component Action required PPE (staff and visitors) Hand hygiene Plastic apron Surgical mask Patient location Allocation of a single room with own bathroom. Door to the room to remain closed. If a patient is located in a shared room, place a surgical mask on the patient, close the privacy curtains around the patient and ensure at least 1 metre between patients. Patient must be moved into a single room as soon as possible. Patient equipment Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room. Airborne precautions: For patients isolated with pulmonary tuberculosis, chickenpox or measles. Component Action required PPE (staff and visitors) Hand hygiene N95 mask Patient location Allocation of a negative pressure isolation room with anteroom. Both sets of doors are to be kept closed to maintain the negative pressure. Patient equipment Dedicated equipment for the length of stay is preferred. If equipment is shared, cleaning is performed between patients as per standard precautions. Patient charts are to remain outside of the patient room. Upon patient discharge The room should remain in negative pressure for a minimum of 30 minutes of the patient leaving. If any staff are entering the room within this 30 minute period, they are to still wear the N95 mask. Click here to download policies
