Term and definitions Authorised person An authorised person is the relevant Manager or the Chief Executive Officer. Employee An employee is a Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student on placement with Bagwan Health. Individual Individual refers to Bagwan Health service users, families and friends, employees, potential employees, volunteers, students and the community. Service user A service user is a child or an adult (person with a disability) or aged person who uses a Bagwan Health service. Workplace Workplace includes working on-site or off-site, attendance at a work-related conference or function, and attendance at a client or other work-related event, including retreats and social events. Policy Bagwan Health supports the rights of all persons covered by the policy to work in an environment that is, so far as is reasonably practicable, safe and without risks to health. Bagwan Health is committed to the promotion of a joint and united approach to consultation and resolution of Work Health and Safety issues, with a view to improving workplace efficiency and productivity. This will be accomplished through the ongoing development, in consultation with Bagwan Health’s Safety Representatives, of management systems and procedures designed to, so far as is reasonably practicable: • identify, assess and control workplace hazards; • reduce the incidence and cost of occupational injury and illness; and • provide a rehabilitation system for those affected by occupational injury or illness. Workplace Occupational Health and Safety statutory requirements, including regulations and codes of practice, are minimum standards and so the aim is for them to be improved upon, where practicable. Procedures Manual handling Bagwan Health follows legislated best practice standards to help create a safe workplace. Bagwan Health refers to detailed Workplace Occupational Health and Safety procedures as set out by Worksafe Victoria’s Health and Safety guides: WorkSafe Victoria — healthcare and hospitals safety basics 1. Working safely in visiting health services: A handbook for workplaces 2. A guide to designing workplaces for safer handling of people 3. Transferring people safely – a handbook for workplaces 4. Transferring people from beds and chairs – A health and safety solution 5. Transferring people for toileting and bathing – A health and safety solution 6. Assisting people who have fallen – A health and safety solution 7. Assisting people in wheelchairs – A health and safety solution 8. Moving and supporting people with a disability – A health and safety solution 9. Re-positioning people in bed – A health and safety solution Health and Safety Committee The Bagwan Health Workplace Occupational Health and Safety Committee should meet at least every three months in a year to monitor and facilitate the development and implementation of Health and Safety Systems, throughout the organisation. Bagwan Health Designated Work Groups are: • Respite & Recreation • Therapy & Inclusion Services • Accommodation & Specialist Support Services • Child & Youth Services • Quality, Innovation & Service Development • People Culture & Resources • Finance • Support Coordination. Each Designated Work Group has at least one OH&S Committee member acting as its Health and Safety Representative. The Program Manager for each Designated Work area is also required to attend the Bagwan Health OH&S Committee meetings. Management should review the relevant legislation to determine whether a Health and Safety Committee is required for the workplace. Management should also consult with the Health and Safety Representatives and the Human Resources Department to determine if a Committee is required at their site. Where a Health and Safety Committee is required by legislation, or where the CEO otherwise deems it necessary, Bagwan Health will establish a Health and Safety Committee. Health and Safety Committee Membership The number of Committee members will be decided and agreed by management, in consultation with employees. Elected health and safety representatives may also be Health and Safety Committee members. At least half of the Health and Safety Committee members must be employee representatives. Health and Safety Committee meetings are to be conducted at least every three months in a year. An agenda will be established prior to the meeting and issued to all persons attending the meeting. Minutes will be taken and forwarded to all Health and Safety Representatives, and copies shall be made available to all employees. Bagwan Health encourages sites to invite appropriate visitors to attend the Occupational Health and Safety meetings and positively contribute. Health and Safety Representative Management must ensure that employee representatives are selected appropriately and that the Committee is established and conducted in accordance with the applicable legislation. The Committee Representatives are required to: • Undertake relevant training, i.e. OH&S Representative Course, to carry the role out effectively • Be aware of the Health and Safety interests of their Designated Work Group, and represent their concerns to their relevant Manager and the Occupational Health & Safety Committee • Attend the OH&S Committee meetings as scheduled. Committee Representatives can conduct Safety Mapping, Site Safety and Vehicle or First Aid Kit Checks and participate in the consultation processes to complete Risk Assessments aiming to best manage safety issues if required. Where required by law, or where deemed necessary, designated workgroups shall each elect a Health and Safety Representative as their elected spokesperson. Health and Safety Representatives are encouraged to work with management to discuss Work Health and Safety issues and to work with management to improve health and safety standards. Dissemination of Policy and Procedure The Workplace Occupational Health & Safety Policy and related procedures will be displayed in the workplace and all employees and volunteers will be provided with a copy by their supervisor/manager. New employees will be provided with a copy of the documents as part of their induction. The policy and related procedures will be reviewed on an annual basis or more frequently, if required, to ensure continued compliance with the relevant legislation. Breach of Workplace Occupational Health and Safety Policy Any breach of this policy may result in counselling and/or disciplinary action, which, in the case of employees, may lead to dismissal, or, in the case of volunteers, may lead to the cessation of their engagement. Any breach of this policy by a contractor may result in the cancellation by Bagwan Health of the services provided by that contractor. Roles and responsibilities Bagwan Health acknowledges that the active cooperation of all managers, employees, volunteers’ students and service users is required for ensuring a safe and healthy working environment. Consequently, the management of Bagwan Health is committed to a consultative approach to Workplace Occupational Health and Safety. All Bagwan Health employees, volunteers and students are expected to contribute to the improvement of health and safety within the workplace and to help facilitate cooperation on health and safety issues and to ensuring health and safety measures are implemented. CEO and other executives The CEO and other executive officers will: • be committed to the provision and maintenance of a healthy and safe workplace • consult and participate in the health and safety program • use risk identification, assessment and control principles to reach Bagwan Health’s health and safety objectives • inform and train all persons to whom this procedure applies in relevant policies, procedures and health and safety obligations • participate in Bagwan Health’s inductions and implement all safety procedures. Human Resources The Human Resources Department will: • be committed to the provision and maintenance of a healthy and safe workplace • ensure that all staff receive the appropriate training in the policy and related procedures, and their obligations under occupational health and safety laws. Supervisors and Managers Supervisors/managers will: • be committed to the provision and maintenance of a healthy and safe workplace • consult and participate in the health and safety program • use risk identification, assessment and control principles to reach Bagwan Health’s health and safety objectives • inform and train all staff in relevant policies, procedures and health and safety obligations • participate in Bagwan Health inductions and implement all safety procedures. Employees Employees will: • participate in health and safety training, actions and activities and support Bagwan Health in its efforts to reach its health and safety and, where relevant, rehabilitation objectives • follow reasonable health and safety instructions from managers or supervisors; • report any serious incidents, accidents, injuries or hazards in the workplace to supervisors or designated representatives • aim to work in a way that does not endanger the health or safety of themselves or others • properly use and maintain safety equipment • make sure visitors follow safety rules in the workplace • participate in Bagwan Health induction programs and implement all detailed safety procedures • assess risks to their health and safety arising from the provision of their service • have control measures in place to address those risks, including complying with any relevant Bagwan Health policies and practices. Health and Safety Committee The role of the Health and Safety Committee is to: • assist in the development, monitoring and review of health and safety policies and procedures • consider any proposal for, or changes to the workplace, policies, work practices or procedures which may affect the health and safety of employees • promote the importance of health and safety amongst management and employees • monitor Bagwan Health’s health and safety performance • monitor the rehabilitation of injured employees • assist in the resolution of health and safety disputes. The Committee will meet on a quarterly basis, or more frequently if required. An agenda will be circulated by the Head of the Committee prior to the meeting. A sample agenda can be found in Appendix B to this procedure. A designated note-taker will take minutes of the meeting. A sample minutes document can be found in Appendix A to this procedure. Health and Safety Representatives The role of Health and Safety Representatives is to: • represent employees from their workgroup in relation to health and safety matters • investigate health and safety-related complaints prior to representations to management • make representations to management and report back to employees on any matter relating to health and safety • discuss with the employees, any proposals or matters which may affect the health and safety of employees • assist management in the identification of hazards, the assessment of risks and implementation of risk control measures • assist in promoting adherence to health and safety policies and procedures • assist in the monitoring of risk controls and health and safety policies and procedures. Forms and templates Please refer to the following forms and templates: • Sample Minutes – Health and Safety Committee Meeting • Sample Agenda – Health and Safety Committee Meeting Click here to download policies

Policy and Procedure Privacy

Version Number 001

Scope and purpose

Bagwan Health is committed to protecting the privacy of personal information which the organisation collects, holds and administers. Personal information is information which directly or indirectly identifies a person.

The purpose of this policy is to provide a framework to protect personal, sensitive and health information of Bagwan Health service users, families and friends, employees, potential employees, volunteers, students and the community, whilst ensuring the delivery of quality service.

Contents

Terms and definitions

Individual refers to Bagwan Health service users, families and friends, employees, potential employees, volunteers, students and the community.

An authorised person is the relevant Manager or the Chief Executive Officer.

Employee is a Bagwan Health employee, volunteer or student on placement with Bagwan Health.

A service user is a child or an adult (person with a disability) or aged person who uses a Bagwan Health service.

Bagwan Health is the reference to the relevant public health organisations and all other organisations under the control and direction of the Minister for Health or the Secretary of Health.

Employee Records consists of Personal Information contained in any records, documents, files and reports that relate to a Bagwan Health employee, potential employee, volunteer or student, such as:

●personal and emergency contacts and next of kin details

●financial affairs, superannuation details, taxation and banking information.

●hours of work, salary and wages

●training, development and performance records.

●disciplining, resignation or termination

●contracts, agreements, terms and conditions of employment.

●correspondence

●photographs

●computer files and email.

Records/files can take many forms besides those often considered as formal.

For example, diary entries, a verbal recollection, comments and notes made in communication books or meeting minutes can all be classified as records.

Employee Sensitive and Health Information consists of any records, documents, files and reports that relate to a Bagwan Health employee, potential employee, volunteer or student, such as:

●Racial or ethnic origin.

●Political opinions or membership of a political association.

●Membership of a professional or trade association or trade union.

●Religious or philosophical beliefs or affiliations.

●Sexual preferences or practices.

●Criminal records and information, note that these documents may be destroyed, following assessment, per the relevant Program Funding Body requirements

●Information regarding their health or disability.

●Their expressed wishes about their future provisions of health services.

●A health service provided, or to be provided or information provided about health services.

Any of the above information may be recorded in Medical Certificates, Workcover Documents, Professional Development and Support Session notes, Education Background Information or Resume Affiliations and must be protected under the Victorian Health Records Act 2001.

Service user records must be protected under the Victorian Health Records Act 2001 and record management is consistent with the Public Records Act 1973.

Service user records can consist of all documents, files and reports that relate to a Bagwan Health service user.

This includes:

●personal and emergency contacts and next of kin details

●racial or ethnic origin

●religious or philosophical beliefs

●case notes

●tape, DVD and video recordings

●computer files and email

●photographs

●financial details

●health Care Plans and other health information

●behaviour and Active Support Plans

●incident reports and;

●other written records.

Privacy policy

Bagwan Health collects and administers a range of personal information that is reasonably necessary for one or more of its functions/activities or services/programs or if this is required by Australian law or a court/tribunal order.

The organisation is committed to protecting the privacy of personal information it collects, holds and administers.

Bagwan Health recognises the essential right of individuals to have their information administered in ways which they would reasonably expect – protected on one hand and made accessible to them on the other.

These privacy values are reflected in and supported by our core values and philosophies which are reflected in our Privacy Policy, which is compliant with the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth).

Bagwan Health is bound by laws which impose specific obligations when it comes to handling information. The organisation has adopted the following principles contained as minimum standards concerning handling personal information.

Bagwan Health will:

Collect only information which the organisation requires for its primary function;

Ensure that service users and employees are informed as to why we collect information and how we administer the information gathered;

Use and disclose personal information only for our primary functions or a directly related purpose, or for another purpose with the person’s consent;

Store personal information securely, protecting it from unauthorised access; and

Provide service users and employees with access to their information, and the right to seek its correction.

Procedures

Collection

Bagwan Health collects service user information only where it is necessary for:

the delivery of effective and efficient service provision to the service user (and their family where applicable)

the mandatory data requirements required by the funding body.

Information will be collected according to service policy and procedures documents and will only be used for the primary purpose intended. If Bagwan Health wishes to use or disclose the information for another purpose (secondary purpose) the individual needs to give consent for this.

Bagwan Health will request information from the service user or, with the knowledge of the service user, from their authorised representative. Service user consent will be obtained and documented before another source being contacted for relevant information.

Bagwan Health will:

Notify service users and employees about why we collect the information and how it is administered.

Notify service users and employees that this information is accessible to them.

Collect personal information from the person themselves wherever possible.

If collecting personal information from a third party, be able to advise the person whom the information concerns, from whom their personal information has been collected.

Collect Sensitive information only with the person’s consent. (Sensitive information includes health information and information about religious beliefs, race, gender and others).

Determine, where unsolicited information is received, whether the personal information could have collected it in the usual way, and then if it could have, it will be treated normally. (If it could not have been, it must be destroyed, and the person whose personal information has been destroyed will be notified about the receipt and destruction of their personal information).

Use and disclosure

Bagwan Health will:

Only use or disclose information for the primary purpose for which it was collected or a directly related secondary purpose

For other uses, Bagwan Health will obtain consent from the affected person

Concerning a secondary purpose, use or disclose personal information only where:

a secondary purpose is related to the primary purpose and the individual would reasonably have expected us to use it for purposes; or

the person has consented; or

certain other legal reasons exist, or disclosure is required to prevent a serious and imminent threat to life, health or safety.

Concerning personal information which has been collected from a person, use the personal information for direct marketing, where that person would reasonably expect it to be used for this purpose, and [organisation] has provided an opt-out and the opt-out has not been taken up.

Concerning personal information which has been collected other than from the person themselves, only use the personal information for direct marketing if the person whose personal information has been collected has consented (and they have not taken up the opt-out).

State in Bagwan Health’s privacy policy whether the information is sent overseas and further will ensure that any overseas providers of services are as compliant with privacy as Bagwan Health is required to be.

Provide all individuals access to personal information except where it is a threat to life or health or it is authorized by law to refuse and, if a person can establish that the personal information is not accurate, then Bagwan Health must take steps to correct it. Bagwan Health may allow a person to attach a statement to their information if Bagwan Health disagrees it is inaccurate.

Where for a legal or other reason we are not required to provide a person with access to the information, consider whether a mutually agreed intermediary would allow enough access to meet the needs of both parties.

Make no charge for requesting personal information, correcting the information or associating a statement regarding accuracy with the personal information.

Storage

Bagwan Health will:

Implement and maintain steps to ensure that personal information is protected from misuse and loss, unauthorized access, interference, unauthorized modification or disclosure.

Before Bagwan Health discloses any personal information to an overseas recipient including a provider of IT services such as servers or cloud services, establish that they are privacy compliant. Bagwan health will have systems which provide enough security.

Ensure that Bagwan Health’s data is up to date, accurate and complete.

Destruction and de-identification

Bagwan Health will:

Ensure that Bagwan Health data is up to date, accurate and complete.

Implement and maintain steps to ensure that personal information is protected from misuse and loss, unauthorized access, interference, unauthorized modification or disclosure.

Before Bagwan Health discloses any personal information to an overseas recipient including a provider of IT services such as servers or cloud services, establish that they are privacy compliant. Bagwan Health will have systems which provide enough security.

Any information relating to service users, employees, volunteers or students, such as correspondence or reports, that are not required to be filed, must be destroyed via the confidential document disposal bag located in the offices.

When an employee, volunteer, student or service user exits or completes their service provision with Bagwan Health, their files and records will be closed and archived for at least 7 years. After this time the file and records will be shredded or securely destroyed.

Comply with the Privacy Act, Employees leaving Greendale Community are required to return, destroy or delete any Greendale Community information they may have in their possession. This includes information stored on their phones and emails etc.

Data quality and security

Bagwan Health will:

take reasonable steps to ensure the information Bagwan Health collects is accurate, complete, up to date, and relevant to the functions we perform

only destroy records according to Bagwan Health’s Record Management Policy.

Access and correction

Bagwan Health will:

Ensure employees, service users, and the public are aware of Bagwan Health’s Privacy Policy and its purposes. Make this information freely available in relevant publications and on the organisation’s website.

Ensure that all records are accurate, up to date, complete and not misleading and will take all reasonable steps to ensure this.

Ensure individuals have a right to seek access to information held about them and to correct it if it is inaccurate, incomplete, misleading or not up to date.

Employees, volunteers, students and service users may request the correction of information or have their dissent regarding any of their personal information recorded.

Allow people from whom the personal information is being collected to not identify themselves or use a pseudonym unless it is impracticable to deal with them on this basis.

Complaints and notification

Complaints by any individual about a breach of the Australian Privacy Principles, or a registered APP code (if any) that binds Bagwan Health are dealt with through the Bagwan Health’s Complaints Policy and procedures.

Privacy breaches are reported to the relevant funding body.

DHHS and NDIS privacy breaches/incidents need to be submitted to DHHS using the web-based Privacy Incident Report form.

For information: https://dhhs.vic.gov.au/publications/privacy-policy

The Notifiable Data Breaches (NDB) scheme requires Bagwan Health to notify the Australian Information Commissioner (the Commissioner) about ‘eligible data breaches’.

A data breach is eligible if it is likely to result in serious harm to any of the individuals to whom the information relates.

For details see https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy-law/privacy-act/notifiable-data-breaches-scheme

Roles and responsibilities

Records and files may be created about an individual associated with Bagwan Health, such as a service user, employee, volunteer or student etc., their records and files are legally owned by the organisation.

Bagwan Health recognises that, with this ownership, comes responsibility for the handling, treatment and access entitlements of the information.

All Employees are responsible for applying and complying with the Privacy standards. Managers are responsible for ensuring that the Employees who they supervise are aware of and understand their responsibilities under the Privacy policy.

Bagwan Health is responsible for developing, adopting and reviewing this policy.

Bagwan Health’s CEO is responsible for the implementation of this policy, for monitoring changes in Privacy legislation, and for advising on the need to review or revise this policy as and when the need arises.

Bagwan Health

Bagwan Health acknowledges its responsibilities in protecting any personal information it has collected and, or has in its keeping, from misuse, modification, loss or unauthorised access and will take all reasonable steps to do so.

At such time that files, records or information are no longer required, Bagwan Health takes all reasonable steps to destroy or de-identify them.

Employees are made aware of Bagwan Health Privacy Policy during their induction (and need to be fully aware that any employee who fails to comply with this policy may be subject to disciplinary action). Furthermore, employees sign-off in their contract that they will abide by this policy.

When employees, volunteers and students support service users with their personal

care needs they will protect their dignity.

Service Managers

Service Managers are responsible for ensuring that employees, volunteers, students and service users who have exited their programs have their records and files archived and stored in a lockable location.

Employees

Employees, volunteers and students must always respect the confidentiality of service users. Service user files and any information relating to service users, must always be stored in a lockable cabinet and must not be removed from the workplace, where it is stored, without authorisation from the relevant Service Manager, and, whenever possible, in a locked case/satchel.

When service user files have been authorised for removal from the workplace, they should be de-identified if possible and kept in the locked boot of a vehicle, whenever possible.

Employees, volunteers and students must not access/view service user files of family members (incl. children, parents or siblings), e.g. protected participants (NDIS definition) as there needs to be a separation between service delivery and the family.

Filing cabinets must be locked by the last employee to leave the service area each day.

Only Bagwan Health employees with appropriate clearance have access to service user files and reports stored on computer and central data.

Bagwan Health Volunteers and Students are also required to comply with the Bagwan Health Privacy Policy. They receive this information and discuss its relevance to their role during their induction.

Employees leaving Bagwan Health are responsible for complying with the Privacy Act and the Australian Privacy Principles for deleting, disposing of or returning any service user information they may have in their possession. This includes their photos or information on their mobile phones, computers etc.

They are also responsible for returning anything that may belong to Bagwan Health, such as keys, I.D. Photos etc.

For details see https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy-law/privacy-act/notifiable-data-breaches-scheme Roles and responsibilities Records and files may be created about an individual associated with Bagwan Health, such as a service user, employee, volunteer or student etc., their records and files are legally owned by the organisation. Bagwan Health recognises that, with this ownership, comes responsibility for the handling, treatment and access entitlements of the information. All Employees are responsible for applying and complying with the Privacy standards. Managers are responsible for ensuring that the Employees who they supervise are aware of and understand their responsibilities under the Privacy policy. Bagwan Health is responsible for developing, adopting and reviewing this policy. Bagwan Health’s CEO is responsible for the implementation of this policy, for monitoring changes in Privacy legislation, and for advising on the need to review or revise this policy as and when the need arises. Bagwan Health Bagwan Health acknowledges its responsibilities in protecting any personal information it has collected and, or has in its keeping, from misuse, modification, loss or unauthorised access and will take all reasonable steps to do so. At such time that files, records or information are no longer required, Bagwan Health takes all reasonable steps to destroy or de-identify them. Employees are made aware of Bagwan Health Privacy Policy during their induction (and need to be fully aware that any employee who fails to comply with this policy may be subject to disciplinary action). Furthermore, employees sign-off in their contract that they will abide by this policy. When employees, volunteers and students support service users with their personal care needs they will protect their dignity. Service Managers Service Managers are responsible for ensuring that employees, volunteers, students and service users who have exited their programs have their records and files archived and stored in a lockable location. Employees Employees, volunteers and students must always respect the confidentiality of service users. Service user files and any information relating to service users, must always be stored in a lockable cabinet and must not be removed from the workplace, where it is stored, without authorisation from the relevant Service Manager, and, whenever possible, in a locked case/satchel. When service user files have been authorised for removal from the workplace, they should be de-identified if possible and kept in the locked boot of a vehicle, whenever possible. Employees, volunteers and students must not access/view service user files of family members (incl. children, parents or siblings), e.g. protected participants (NDIS definition) as there needs to be a separation between service delivery and the family. Filing cabinets must be locked by the last employee to leave the service area each day. Only Bagwan Health employees with appropriate clearance have access to service user files and reports stored on computer and central data. Bagwan Health Volunteers and Students are also required to comply with the Bagwan Health Privacy Policy. They receive this information and discuss its relevance to their role during their induction. Employees leaving Bagwan Health are responsible for complying with the Privacy Act and the Australian Privacy Principles for deleting, disposing of or returning any service user information they may have in their possession. This includes their photos or information on their mobile phones, computers etc. They are also responsible for returning anything that may belong to Bagwan Health, such as keys, I.D. Photos etc.

Policy Name

Specimen Storage and Collection

Policy Number

010

Owner of Policy

Dr Christina Jones, CEO

Scope

All staff and contractors employed by Bagwan Health, Allied Health professionals, Credentialed Specialists and students who are responsible for collecting and/or storing specimens.

 

Policy 

The National Pathology Accreditation Advisory Council (NPAAC), the Royal College of Pathologists of Australasia (RCPA) and the Consumers Health Forum of Australia (CHF) identified the need for appropriate and documented specimen storage and collection processes as a high priority area where promoting best practice could lead to better patient outcomes.

This policy defines the standards and processes associated with the collection and storage of specimens at Bagwan Health.

 

Procedure

Pathology tests are an essential part of the health care system and are used to aid medical practitioners in the diagnosis of disease, assist in preventive health, acute care, management of chronic conditions and genetic research.

Pathology specimens provide essential information that assists patient management including determining appropriate treatment, which influences clinical outcomes of patients.

For the purposes of this policy, a specimen is any tissue or fluid from a patient that is submitted to Bagwan Health or external agency for analysis or testing. 

This can include, but is not limited to:

• Blood

• Urine

• Throat swabs

• Tissue biopsies

• Sputum

• Bodily fluids

• Faecal matter.

 

Request Forms for Testing

Bagwan Health provides request forms that must be completed for testing along with the supplies to collect the specimens. A request form must accompany each specimen. In order to provide accurate service, the request form and labels must be completed as described below.

 

Minimum Labelling Requirements

All patient information on the request form must match the patient information on the specimen labels. To comply with National Safety and Quality Health Service (NSQHS) standards, pathology request forms and specimens MUST have three identifiers:

• Patient’s full name – first name, surname and any middle names

• MRN or another unique patient identifier

• Date of Birth (DOB).

 

Clinical information must also be provided and will assist with determining the level of investigation required and the importance and prioritisation of unexpected results.

Labelling may include clinical details such as:

• Current problem

• Differential diagnosis

• Relevant medical history.

 

Contact details for the referrer must also be supplied for each request, this includes:

• Legible referrer name 

• Contact details e.g. phone number.

 

Note: If there is no label or the label is incomplete there will be no testing.

 

Specimen Relabelling

Specimen relabelling is not permitted. National Association of Testing Authorities (NATA) requirements reflect a tight policy on specimen relabelling. Since 1 October 2012, re-labelling of specimens has not been permitted.

Compliance will ensure maximum patient safety is a priority.

 

Specimen Relabelling

Pathology will not accept specimens that are unlabelled, mislabelled, mismatched or insufficiently labelled.

This is because unlabelled, mismatched or mislabelled specimens are the main sources of pre-analytical errors in the laboratory.

These types of errors can result in:

• Adverse patient outcomes including misdiagnosis and delayed, omitted or incorrect treatment

• Incorrect type of blood product being administered to the patient, which could lead to patient death

• Poor patient experience for patients who require a second sample to be recollected or the loss of the irreplaceable specimen

• Delays in forensic investigations and reports to families and coronial authorities.

Exceptions

For unidentifiable or unconscious patients, a minimum of two (2) patient identifiers must be used. This might include:

• MRN or other patient identifiers

• A further descriptor, for example, patient gender, motorbike accident.

Cases of unknown ID, or ID in situ, are managed by Victoria Police in the first instance. If a specimen is taken for the purposes of ID, the normal procedure for unknown or unidentified samples must be followed. In this case, other identifiers are used such as gender or a unique identifier.

 

Health and Safety Precautions

Specimens must be handled in a safe manner and according to applicable legal requirements. Use precautions when handling specimens containing blood or other potentially infectious material. Work areas contaminated with blood or serum must be disinfected immediately with 10% bleach (hypochlorite at 0.5% final concentration) or other approved disinfectant.

In the event of an exposure, administer first aid immediately, notify your manager or supervisor and seek prompt medical attention. First aid includes washing cuts and needle sticks with soap and water; flushing splashes to the nose, mouth, or skin with copious amounts of water; and irrigating eyes with clean water, saline, or sterile irrigants.

 

Collection a Specimen

Proper specimen collection and handling is an integral part of obtaining a valid and timely laboratory test result. Specimens must be obtained in the proper tubes or containers, correctly labelled, and then promptly transported to the laboratory.

The following steps are to collect a specimen for a patient:

1. Use the patient chart to confirm the patient’s identity and if applicable, scan the patient’s wristband using the barcode scanner.

2. Refer to the system to check what specimens were ordered.

3. Print the applicable specimen labels using the system.

4. Promptly collect labels from the printer.

5. Once the specimens are in their containers, initial and time and date the label/s.

6. Affix the appropriate label to the correct collection container. The barcode must be horizontal and straight, and over the existing label.

7. To communicate if the patient is fasting or if the specimen is urgent/critical, use the appropriate stickers and attach to the lid of the specimen. Write any additional comments relating to the collection on the specimen label or on a note placed in the specimen bag with the container.

8. Use the barcode scanner to scan the labels attached to the specimen containers. The system will confirm that the patient chart and the specimen container label are matched to the correct patient. The specimen order will be displayed with a tick to indicate it has been collected.

9. If a barcode scanner is not available it will be necessary to manually change the collected status of each of the specimens in the system. This can be done via the Status Menu in the system.

10. A warning message will display as the label was not scanned. Click ‘Yes’ once you have verified the container and label.

11. Marking specimens as Collected in the system will create an entry in AUSLAB for the tests indicated on the label.

12. Close system and send specimens to pathology.

 

Obtaining Reliable and Accurate Laboratory Test Results

Doctors and others responsible for obtaining specimens and transporting them to the laboratory have a vital role in ensuring that laboratory test results are valid. 

The following are essential safeguards for your patients:

• Avoid patient identification errors. Identify the patient prior to collecting a specimen using at least two patient identifiers. This could also be done by checking armbands. Acceptable identifiers may include the patient’s full name, date of birth, or medical record number.

• If applicable, draw the tubes in the proper sequence. When multiple tubes are to be drawn from a single venipuncture using an evacuated tube system, there is a correct sequence for blood collection that prevents cross-contamination of tube additives that could cause erroneous test results. The following should be used for both plastic and glass blood collection tubes. First collect blood in plain tubes, followed by gel tubes, then, liquid additive tubes.

• Use proper containers for collection. Using the wrong container often leads to erroneous results. Refer to the Swab Collection Guide and the Tube Collection Guide for exact requirements.

• Do not decant specimens from one type of container into another. Specimens must be submitted to the laboratory in the container used originally for collection.

• Promptly organise delivery of the specimens to the laboratory.

 

The Handling and Storage of Specimens 

Specimens should be stored and transported in a manner which maintains the viability of the specimen for the lifetime of the request. Generally, the specimen requirements are written in a format that specifies the requested volume, storage temperature, and any special handling notes. Blood tests that are required to be placed on ice, such as an arterial blood gas, must be taken immediately to the laboratory by a staff member, and not sent by the collection chute.

The requested volume is an amount sufficient to allow at least two performances of the assay either singly or in duplicate. The minimum volume allows one single analysis including instrument dead volume. 

Storage temperature is specified as room temperature (15 – 30°C), refrigerated (2 to 10°C) or frozen (-20°C or colder). When the temperature is not indicated, the sample may be stored and shipped in the most convenient manner. 

 

Download the supplied specimen storage and collection policy.

pages.html:
Policy Name Training and Development

Owner of Policy –  George Dunn Executive Director of People and Culture

Scope

This policy applies to employees working for Bagwan Health who are:

  • Current employees
  • New permanent, temporary or casual
  • Existing employees appointed, promoted or transferred to another work location
  • Existing employees resuming duty after leave of more than 12 months.

This policy also applies to contractors, consultants, students and volunteers where there is a legislative requirement for specific training. This training requirement is to be included in contract arrangements, and the training must occur. This policy does not apply to Victorian Ambulance Service employees.  

Policy

The purpose of this policy is to facilitate the training and development of staff as part of their employment and to provide administrative guidelines to facilitate fairness and equity in the application of these guidelines. Every effort has been made to balance the needs of staff for professional development, the needs of the organisation for properly qualified staff, and the need to staff the Bagwan Health’s services. This policy defines the standards and processes associated with training and development at Bagwan Health and has been developed by the Bagwan Health Office in consultation with the Training and Development Committee and the Executive of each site/service.

Procedure

Orientation, Induction and Mandatory Training

Within three months of commencing employment at Bagwan Health, unless stated otherwise, every employee is required to undertake the following training:

  • Bagwan Health orientation training
  • Local orientation training
  • Local induction training
  • Mandatory training

Orientation and Induction Training

Orientation and Induction training programs occur in the first few days of a new employee joining Bagwan Health. As such they are often confused for the same training, but it is easy to differentiate between the two. Orientation training is used to welcome employees to the organisation and to provide information about the organisation’s mission, strategic objectives, corporate initiatives and specific information including structure and scope of operations. Orientation training contains both workplace and organisational elements. Induction training is used to familiarise employees with their work unit and to provide information about local work practices, standards, safe work procedures, administrative procedures and training in relevant systems. It may also include some mandatory training. Some topics may be included in both orientation and induction, as they require both a local and a broader application. Existing employees who are transferred, seconded or promoted into another division are to be included in the local orientation (and/or refresher program) and local induction.

Mandatory Training

Mandatory training is compulsory for all employees regardless of their role or location, and is mandated by relevant:

  • Commonwealth or state legislation
  • Administrative policy
  • Code of practice or regulation linked to legislation
  • Directives
  • Bagwan Health HR policies
  • Service Level Agreements

Mandatory Training for Specific Groups

Training can be deemed compulsory for a specific group of employees, but not be required for all employees within Bagwan Health. This type of training may be mandatory due to location, occupation, speciality, work unit, or based upon risk assessment processes. If there is occupation based mandatory training that must be completed prior to taking on specific duties (e.g. nursing and medication administration), the employee cannot perform those duties until their training is completed and they are deemed competent. All completed mandatory training must be recorded and signed off on a checklist for reporting and monitoring purposes.

Mandatory Training for Temporary or Casual Employees

Temporary and casual employees engaged for less than three months are to complete mandatory training. However, the required learning topics of the Bagwan Health and local orientation may be modified to reflect the role and length of employment of the temporary/casual employee.

Professional Development

Bagwan Health acknowledges that professional development is integral to personal job satisfaction, workplace productivity, reward, and recognition, and is critical to the achievement of the organisation’s mission to continuously improve the quality of its programs and services. Professional development programs include on-the-job training, career development and transition programs, internal or external courses, support for undertaking research or project work, support for participation in internal or external governance processes, attendance at conferences or seminars, and networking, coaching and mentoring programs. Bagwan Health is committed to providing employees with:

  • The opportunity to plan and develop skills, knowledge and attributes that complement organisational and work unit goals
  • The opportunity to participate in career development activities that extend and enhance their capabilities and capacity for advancement within the organisation
  • Equity of access to professional development opportunities

Great professional development is:

  • Targeted
  • Available as needed
  • Available to all staff
  • Evaluated
  • Accessible
  • Preferably in-house
  • Includes on-the-job and ongoing supervision

Strategies for Professional Development

The strategies used to implement professional development at Bagwan Health include:

  1. Annual performance review to set staff training and development objectives
  2. Regular quality in-service education programs, where professionals are trained and discuss their work with others in their peer group
  3. Organised formal professional clinical supervision and teaching programs
  4. Organisational priorities for staff development
  5. Guidelines on staff attendance at external training
  6. Annual update of organisational staff development priority lists
  7. Annual allocation of staff development budget
  8. Quarterly review of staff development expenditure
  9. Annual report on all staff development activities undertaken in previous year
  10. A centralised training database to provide quarterly staff reports on attendance
  11. Time allocation guidelines to quality-research-evaluation program development

Position-specific Professional Development

Where management decides that it is necessary for a staff member to acquire a particular skill, to learn specific material, or to acquire specific qualifications in order for them to carry out the duties attached to their current role, Bagwan Health is responsible for all costs incurred in acquiring that skill, learning or qualification, and the staff member shall, where necessary, be given permission to attend any such course within working hours. It is expected that such requirements would have been taken into account in the writing of a role description and were included in the criteria for selection. Thus it would rarely be the case that continuing employees would be required to acquire new qualifications.

Non-position-specific Professional Development

There may be instances where an employee wishes to pursue further education or training but management has not required them to acquire a particular skill, to learn specific material, or to gain specific qualifications to carry out duties attached to their current role. In these cases, Bagwan Health (at the discretion of management and taking into account workplace efficiency), may assist such training by allowing the employee to:

  • Rearrange current working hours
  • Use Bagwan Health equipment and services
  • Use annual leave or unpaid leave arrangements
  • Grant up to two days study leave to attend examinations.

A reimbursement of training fees or provision of paid study leave may also be negotiated as part of the contract of employment between the employee and Bagwan Health.

Budgeting

It is the responsibility of the Bagwan Health Board to authorise an appropriate annual expenditure budget to facilitate appropriate professional development opportunities for employees. It shall be the responsibility of management to ensure that employees are offered and granted appropriate professional development opportunities, taking into account the needs of the individual as well as the organisation.

Proposals for Professional Development

As part of their performance review, employees will be encouraged to take an active role in their own ongoing professional and career development. Any proposal by an employee for a change in their existing conditions of employment (hours of work, taking of leave, use of equipment, etc.) to facilitate their professional development shall be considered by the management as subject to:

Bagwan Health policy to encourage such development

The training priorities of Bagwan Health Satisfactory assurances from that person’s manager that business can still be carried on satisfactorily Equity in the provision of such facilitation between employees Any such agreement shall be fully documented in that person’s personnel file.

Bagwan Health Training Packages

Management are encouraged to use existing Bagwan Health online and face-to-face training packages to ensure consistency of information delivered to employees, especially in regards to compliance related training. These packages have been developed to comply with legislation, policies and directives.

Training Delivery and Modulation

Employee needs must be taken into consideration when selecting training delivery methods. Bagwan Health training may use any of the following:

  • Face-to-face delivery
  • Online delivery
  • CD/DVD information
  • Video presentation
  • One-on-one in-service information sharing
  • Accessible electronic delivery e.g. closed caption, assistive technology

. The location and time of training must be considered to ensure that all employees are able to attend e.g. shift workers, part-time employees, employees with special learning needs, physical impairments and/or disabilities.

Reporting, Monitoring and Compliance

Management is responsible for managing compliance of mandatory training of employees under their supervision. Management must also ensure that employee details are registered in the appropriate learning management system for reporting, monitoring and compliance.

Non-position-specific Professional Development There may be instances where an employee wishes to pursue further education or training but management has not required them to acquire a particular skill, to learn specific material, or to gain specific qualifications to carry out duties attached to their current role. In these cases, Bagwan Health (at the discretion of management and taking into account workplace efficiency), may assist such training by allowing the employee to: Rearrange current working hours Use Bagwan Health equipment and services Use annual leave or unpaid leave arrangements Grant up to two days study leave to attend examinations. A reimbursement of training fees or provision of paid study leave may also be negotiated as part of the contract of employment between the employee and Bagwan Health. Budgeting It is the responsibility of the Bagwan Health Board to authorise an appropriate annual expenditure budget to facilitate appropriate professional development opportunities for employees. It shall be the responsibility of management to ensure that employees are offered and granted appropriate professional development opportunities, taking into account the needs of the individual as well as the organisation. Proposals for Professional Development As part of their performance review, employees will be encouraged to take an active role in their own ongoing professional and career development. Any proposal by an employee for a change in their existing conditions of employment (hours of work, taking of leave, use of equipment, etc.) to facilitate their professional development shall be considered by the management as subject to: Bagwan Health policy to encourage such development The training priorities of Bagwan Health Satisfactory assurances from that person’s manager that business can still be carried on satisfactorily Equity in the provision of such facilitation between employees Any such agreement shall be fully documented in that person’s personnel file. Bagwan Health Training Packages Management are encouraged to use existing Bagwan Health online and face-to-face training packages to ensure consistency of information delivered to employees, especially in regards to compliance related training. These packages have been developed to comply with legislation, policies and directives. Training Delivery and Modulation Employee needs must be taken into consideration when selecting training delivery methods. Bagwan Health training may use any of the following: Face-to-face delivery Online delivery CD/DVD information Video presentation One-on-one in-service information sharing Accessible electronic delivery e.g. closed caption, assistive technology . The location and time of training must be considered to ensure that all employees are able to attend e.g. shift workers, part-time employees, employees with special learning needs, physical impairments and/or disabilities. Reporting, Monitoring and Compliance Management is responsible for managing compliance of mandatory training of employees under their supervision. Management must also ensure that employee details are registered in the appropriate learning management system for reporting, monitoring and compliance. Click here to download policies

drafts.title: Medication safety
drafts.html:
Purpose and scope

This draft describes medication safety responsibilities for the Bagwan simulation. It applies to the use of medication information in learning scenarios. It does not authorise prescribing, dispensing or administration.

Before proceeding

  • Work within your role, competence and the approved local procedure.
  • Confirm the patient identity and the current medication information provided in the scenario.
  • Check the documented allergy and adverse drug reaction history.
  • Refer discrepancies, missing information or uncertainty to the supervising clinician or pharmacist before proceeding.

Documentation and communication

Keep medication information accurate, communicate changes during transitions of care, and record the relevant observations and actions. Use the incident reporting process for a medication incident or near miss.

Approval requirements

The SME must confirm responsibilities, local escalation arrangements, required checks and documentation before this draft is used for teaching. No medicine, dose, administration instruction or checking protocol is specified here.

drafts.title: Nursing and clinical handover
drafts.html:
Purpose

Support a structured transfer of relevant information and responsibility during the Bagwan simulation.

Prepare the handover

Use the handover structure approved for the learning scenario. Check the patient identity against the scenario record. Gather the current situation, relevant background, observations, identified risks, pending actions and the patient's preferences.

Give and receive the handover

  • Identify who is handing over and who will accept responsibility.
  • Communicate accurate, relevant and current information in a logical order.
  • State outstanding actions, who will complete them and when they require attention.
  • Allow questions and confirm shared understanding.
  • Record the handover and clarify any information that remains uncertain.

Approval requirements

The SME must define the required identifiers, handover framework, minimum information and escalation process for each scenario. This draft is a communication framework, not an approved clinical protocol.

drafts.title: Booking an interpreter
drafts.reason: The original page contained an unfilled policy template
drafts.html:
Prepare the request

Confirm the person's preferred language, dialect and communication needs. Identify the appointment time, expected duration, location or remote format, and the purpose of the appointment. Record any preferences or circumstances relevant to selecting an interpreter.

Arrange the service

Use the organisation's approved language service arrangements. Confirm the interpreter's suitability and credentials for the task. Provide the information required for the booking through the approved channel and confirm the arrangements with the patient and the appointment team.

Before the appointment

Plan suitable space, equipment and time. Brief the interpreter on the purpose and relevant context. Check that the patient understands the interpreter's role.

In this simulation

No external booking is sent. Record a proposed booking in your learning evidence and discuss it with your facilitator. The SME must confirm provider arrangements, urgency pathways and documentation requirements before approval.

Proposed service overview

This service page is intended to help staff find culturally appropriate liaison support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander patients and families in Bagwan scenarios.

Discuss the person's needs

Ask about the person's preferences for support and communication. Respect their choice about involving family, support people or a liaison service. Discuss the relevant referral arrangements with the scenario facilitator.

Liaison team

The archived staff directory names Gina Starr, Fiona Phillips, Monti Williams and Merindah Olden. Their formal reporting lines await confirmation.

Service details awaiting confirmation

Available resource

The recovered Closing the Gap video is available in the video library as a discussion resource.

drafts.title: Laboratory PPE reference
drafts.reason: Replace the archived drag activity with an appropriate intranet reference and separate practice
drafts.html:
Use the task risk assessment

Select protective equipment using the approved procedure and the hazards of the task. The original activity's single set of clothing choices does not establish suitable PPE for every laboratory task.

Before work

  • Confirm the task, hazards and approved controls.
  • Check the specified protective clothing, hand protection, eye protection and footwear.
  • Check that equipment fits, is in good condition and is suitable for the task.
  • Clarify any missing instruction with the supervisor before proceeding.

Practical skills

Selection, fit, use and removal require supervised practice. The optional HTML exercise is in the learning guide and does not assess practical competence.

drafts.title: Laboratory waste reference
drafts.reason: The archived answer key categorised unspecified expired medication as cytotoxic waste
drafts.html:
Identify the waste before disposal

Use the current local waste procedure and the labels on the approved containers. Waste classification depends on what the material is and what it is contaminated with.

When information is missing

Do not guess from a picture or container colour. Ask the supervisor to confirm the classification and handling requirements.

Archived activity correction

The original activity described expired medication without specifying its type. That description does not establish that the medication is cytotoxic. The draft practice exercise uses an explicitly identified cytotoxic residue instead. The SME must review every category and example before use.
